{"parentUuid":"8d5e5f53-b993-4dec-923b-e30ec9248a04","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_stluaw8c7ju0m21xyhat6jta","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp5/a/src/vfs.rs","content":"//! Injectable filesystem I/O layer.\n//!\n//! All repository disk access goes through the [`Vfs`] trait. Two\n//! implementations exist:\n//!\n//! * [`StdVfs`] — thin wrapper over `std::fs` used by the real server.\n//! * [`FaultyVfs`] — wraps any inner Vfs and can be armed at runtime to inject\n//!   failures (`io::Error`) or corrupting behavior at specific call sites.\n//!   Fault rules are matched against a string *site* name the repository\n//!   passes on every call (e.g. `\"rename_root\"`), so tests can simulate\n//!   exactly the failure window \"root switch interrupted after the new block\n//!   data was written but before the root pointer is published\".\n//!\n//! Synchronization boundary: a Vfs only performs one filesystem operation at\n//! a time; multi-operation atomicity (temp-file + fsync + rename) is provided\n//! by [`Vfs::write_atomic`]. Cross-process mutual exclusion is out of scope —\n//! one repository process owns a data directory.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::io::{self, Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\n/// Errors the I/O layer can surface.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum VfsError {\n    /// Plain OS-level failure.\n    Io(io::Error),\n    /// Deliberately injected failure from a [`FaultyVfs`] rule.\n    Injected(String),\n}\n\nimpl VfsError {\n    pub fn not_found(msg: &str) -> Self {\n        VfsError::Io(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, msg))\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_not_found(&self) -> bool {\n        match self {\n            VfsError::Io(e) => e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound,\n            VfsError::Injected(_) => false,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for VfsError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            VfsError::Io(e) => write!(f, \"io error: {e}\"),\n            VfsError::Injected(s) => write!(f, \"injected failure: {s}\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for VfsError {}\n\nimpl From<io::Error> for VfsError {\n    fn from(e: io::Error) -> Self {\n        VfsError::Io(e)\n    }\n}\n\npub type VfsResult<T> = Result<T, VfsError>;\n\n/// What a fault rule does when triggered.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum FaultAction {\n    /// Return an `io::Error` of the given kind (default `Other`) and perform\n    /// nothing.\n    Fail,\n    /// Perform the write but corrupt the bytes at a fixed offset first\n    /// (write-only faults; no-op for other operations).\n    CorruptByte { offset: u64, xor: u8 },\n    /// Perform the operation, then return an error anyway (\"write reported a\n    /// failure although the data may have landed\").\n    SucceedThenFail,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct Rule {\n    /// Remaining trigger count; `None` = unlimited.\n    remaining: Option<usize>,\n    action: FaultAction,\n}\n\n/// Thread-safe shared fault configuration.\n#[derive(Clone, Default)]\npub struct FaultMap {\n    inner: Arc<Mutex<BTreeMap<String, Rule>>>,\n}\n\nimpl FaultMap {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Arm a fault at `site`: the next `times` matching calls (or every call\n    /// when `times` is `None`) take `action`.\n    pub fn arm(&self, site: impl Into<String>, action: FaultAction, times: Option<usize>) {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().insert(\n            site.into(),\n            Rule {\n                remaining: times,\n                action,\n            },\n        );\n    }\n\n    pub fn fail_once(&self, site: impl Into<String>) {\n        self.arm(site, FaultAction::Fail, Some(1));\n    }\n\n    pub fn clear(&self, site: &str) {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().remove(site);\n    }\n\n    pub fn clear_all(&self) {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().clear();\n    }\n\n    /// Atomically consume one trigger at `site`, returning the action to run.\n    fn consume(&self, site: &str) -> Option<FaultAction> {\n        let mut map = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let rule = map.get_mut(site)?;\n        if let Some(left) = &mut rule.remaining {\n            if *left == 0 {\n                return None;\n            }\n            *left -= 1;\n        }\n        let action = rule.action.clone();\n        if let Some(left) = rule.remaining {\n            if left == 0 {\n                map.remove(site);\n            }\n        }\n        Some(action)\n    }\n}\n\n/// The injectable filesystem abstraction. Every `site` argument names the\n/// logical call site for fault matching and is ignored by [`StdVfs`].\npub trait Vfs: Send + Sync {\n    fn create_dir_all(&self, path: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<()>;\n    fn read(&self, path: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<Vec<u8>>;\n    fn exists(&self, path: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<bool>;\n    fn remove_file(&self, path: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<()>;\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<()>;\n    fn write_temp_and_rename(\n        &self,\n        temp: &Path,\n        target: &Path,\n        data: &[u8],\n        site: &str,\n    ) -> VfsResult<()>;\n    fn list_dir(&self, path: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<Vec<String>>;\n\n    /// Write `data` to `target` via a sibling temp file, fsync, then atomic\n    /// rename. `site` names the *rename* step; the temp-write step uses\n    /// `\"{site}_tmp\"`. Kept as a provided method so fault behavior composes\n    /// identically over any backend.\n    fn write_atomic(&self, target: &Path, data: &[u8], site: &str) -> VfsResult<()> {\n        let name = target\n            .file_name()\n            .and_then(|n| n.to_str())\n            .unwrap_or(\"tmp\");\n        let temp = target.with_file_name(format!(\".{name}.tmp-{:x}\", pseudo_random()));\n        self.write_temp_and_rename(&temp, target, data, site)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Cheap non-cryptographic entropy for unique temp suffixes (PIDs collide in\n/// tests that run many repos in one process).\nfn pseudo_random() -> u64 {\n    use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\n    static COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);\n    let n = COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)\n        ^ std::process::id() as u64\n        ^ (std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .map(|d| d.subsec_nanos() as u64)\n            .unwrap_or(0));\n    n\n}\n\n// ---------------- StdVfs ----------------\n\npub struct StdVfs;\n\nimpl StdVfs {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        StdVfs\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for StdVfs {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Vfs for StdVfs {\n    fn create_dir_all(&self, path: &Path, _site: &str) -> VfsResult<()> {\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(path)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn read(&self, path: &Path, _site: &str) -> VfsResult<Vec<u8>> {\n        Ok(std::fs::read(path)?)\n    }\n\n    fn exists(&self, path: &Path, _site: &str) -> VfsResult<bool> {\n        Ok(path.exists())\n    }\n\n    fn remove_file(&self, path: &Path, _site: &str) -> VfsResult<()> {\n        std::fs::remove_file(path)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path, _site: &str) -> VfsResult<()> {\n        std::fs::rename(from, to)?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn write_temp_and_rename(\n        &self,\n        temp: &Path,\n        target: &Path,\n        data: &[u8],\n        _site: &str,\n    ) -> VfsResult<()> {\n        {\n            let mut f = std::fs::File::create(temp)?;\n            f.write_all(data)?;\n            f.sync_all()?;\n        }\n        std::fs::rename(temp, target)?;\n        // Best-effort durability of the directory entry itself.\n        if let Ok(dir) = std::fs::File::open(target.parent().unwrap_or(Path::new(\".\"))) {\n            let _ = dir.sync_all();\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn list_dir(&self, path: &Path, _site: &str) -> VfsResult<Vec<String>> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        if !path.exists() {\n            return Ok(out);\n        }\n        for e in std::fs::read_dir(path)? {\n            let e = e?;\n            if let Some(n) = e.file_name().to_str() {\n                out.push(n.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------- FaultyVfs ----------------\n\n/// Wraps another [`Vfs`] and applies rules from a shared [`FaultMap`].\npub struct FaultyVfs {\n    inner: Box<dyn Vfs>,\n    faults: FaultMap,\n}\n\nimpl FaultyVfs {\n    pub fn new(inner: Box<dyn Vfs>, faults: FaultMap) -> Self {\n        FaultyVfs { inner, faults }\n    }\n\n    pub fn faults(&self) -> &FaultMap {\n        &self.faults\n    }\n\n    fn injected(name: &str) -> VfsError {\n        VfsError::Injected(name.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Vfs for FaultyVfs {\n    fn create_dir_all(&self, path: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<()> {\n        if let Some(action) = self.faults.consume(site) {\n            if matches!(action, FaultAction::Fail) {\n                return Err(Self::injected(site));\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.create_dir_all(path, site)\n    }\n\n    fn read(&self, path: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<Vec<u8>> {\n        if let Some(action) = self.faults.consume(site) {\n            if matches!(action, FaultAction::Fail) {\n                return Err(Self::injected(site));\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.read(path, site)\n    }\n\n    fn exists(&self, path: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<bool> {\n        if let Some(action) = self.faults.consume(site) {\n            if matches!(action, FaultAction::Fail) {\n                return Err(Self::injected(site));\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.exists(path, site)\n    }\n\n    fn remove_file(&self, path: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<()> {\n        if let Some(action) = self.faults.consume(site) {\n            if matches!(action, FaultAction::Fail) {\n                return Err(Self::injected(site));\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.remove_file(path, site)\n    }\n\n    fn rename(&self, from: &Path, to: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<()> {\n        match self.faults.consume(site) {\n            Some(FaultAction::Fail) => Err(Self::injected(site)),\n            Some(FaultAction::SucceedThenFail) => {\n                self.inner.rename(from, to, site)?;\n                Err(Self::injected(site))\n            }\n            _ => self.inner.rename(from, to, site),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn write_temp_and_rename(\n        &self,\n        temp: &Path,\n        target: &Path,\n        data: &[u8],\n        site: &str,\n    ) -> VfsResult<()> {\n        // Rename-phase fault: data is fully written and fsynced, then the\n        // publish step fails — the classic \"interrupted root switch\".\n        if let Some(action) = self.faults.consume(site) {\n            match action {\n                FaultAction::Fail => return Err(Self::injected(site)),\n                FaultAction::SucceedThenFail => {\n                    self.inner.write_temp_and_rename(temp, target, data, site)?;\n                    return Err(Self::injected(site));\n                }\n                FaultAction::CorruptByte { .. } => {\n                    // Corruption applies to bytes, so delegate to data path.\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        // Temp-write-phase fault: apply byte corruption or failure before the\n        // inner backend sees the data.\n        let mut owned: Vec<u8>;\n        let data = if let Some(action) = self.faults.consume(&format!(\"{site}_tmp\")) {\n            match action {\n                FaultAction::Fail => return Err(Self::injected(site)),\n                FaultAction::CorruptByte { offset, xor } => {\n                    owned = data.to_vec();\n                    let off = (offset as usize).min(owned.len().saturating_sub(1));\n                    if !owned.is_empty() {\n                        owned[off] ^= xor;\n                    }\n                    &owned[..]\n                }\n                FaultAction::SucceedThenFail => {\n                    self.inner.write_temp_and_rename(temp, target, data, site)?;\n                    return Err(Self::injected(site));\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            data\n        };\n        self.inner.write_temp_and_rename(temp, target, data, site)\n    }\n\n    fn list_dir(&self, path: &Path, site: &str) -> VfsResult<Vec<String>> {\n        if let Some(action) = self.faults.consume(site) {\n            if matches!(action, FaultAction::Fail) {\n                return Err(Self::injected(site));\n            }\n        }\n        self.inner.list_dir(path, site)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Helper used in tests: write-then-read round trip helper kept here so\n/// neither module needs `std::fs` directly in fault scenarios.\n#[allow(dead_code)]\npub fn append_file(path: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n    let mut f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n        .create(true)\n        .append(true)\n Cross-process mutual exclusion is out of scope —\n//! one repository process owns a data directory.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::io::{self, Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\n/// Errors the I/O layer can surface.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum VfsError {\n    /// Plain OS-level failure.\n    Io(io::Error),\n    /// Deliberately injected failure from a [`FaultyVfs`] rule.\n    Injected(String),\n}\n\nimpl VfsError {\n    pub fn not_found(msg: &str) -> Self {\n        VfsError::Io(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, msg))\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_not_found(&self) -> bool {\n        match self {\n            VfsError::Io(e) => e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound,\n            VfsError::Injected(_) => false,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for VfsError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            VfsError::Io(e) => write!(f, \"io error: {e}\"),\n            VfsError::Injected(s) => write!(f, \"injected failure: {s}\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for VfsError {}\n\nimpl From<io::Error> for VfsError {\n    fn from(e: io::Error) -> Self {\n        VfsError::Io(e)\n    }\n}\n\npub type VfsResult<T> = Result<T, VfsError>;\n\n/// What a fault rule does when triggered.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum FaultAction {\n    /// Return an `io::Error` of the given kind (default `Other`) and perform\n    /// nothing.\n    Fail,\n    /// Perform the write but corrupt the bytes at a fixed offset first\n    /// (write-only faults; no-op for other operations).\n    CorruptByte { offset: u64, xor: u8 },\n    /// Perform the operation, then return an error anyway (\"write reported a\n    /// failure although the data may have landed\").\n    SucceedThenFail,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct Rule {\n    /// Remaining trigger count; File-backed content-addressable block store.\n//!\n//! ## Disk format (version 1)\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! <data-dir>/\n//!   VERSION                       # contains \"cas-repo v1\\n\"\n//!   blocks/\n//!     <aa>/                       # first byte of the digest, 256 shards\n//!       <rest-62-hex>             # immutable blob: exact block bytes\n//!       <rest-62-hex>.refs.json   # sidecar: {\"version\":1,\"refs\":[\"<sha256>\", ...]}\n//!       .<...>.tmp-<rand>         # staging files (atomic rename source)\n//!   roots/\n//!     <name>.json                 # {\"hash\":\"<sha256>\",\"version\":N,\"updated_at_ms\":T}\n//!     .<name>.json.tmp-<rand>     # staging files\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Invariants:\n//! * Blob bytes always hash to their path digest. Hash is verified on read and\n//!   during GC marking; it is an integrity check only, never an access token.\n//! * Blobs are immutable: a `put` of an existing digest never rewrites the\n//!   blob, only unions the declared reference set.\n//! * A root pointer appears via one temp-file + fsync + rename step, so root\n//!   updates are atomic: readers see either the old or the new version.\n//!\n//! ## Synchronization boundary\n//!\n//! One store object owns one data directory (single process). Internally:\n//! * `upload` serializes puts of the *same* staging paths;\n//! * a `RwLock` guards root-pointer changes against GC;\n//! * the pin table counts in-flight readers and GC-live blocks. Sweep checks\n//!   the pin count and deletes while holding the pin lock, closing the\n//!   reader/GC and uploader/GC windows.\n\nuse std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, RwLock};\n\nuse crate::hash::Sha256;\nuse crate::json::Json;\nuse crate::vfs::{VfsError, VfsResult, Vfs};\n\nconst FORMAT_VERSION_LINE: &str = \"cas-repo v1\\n\";\n/// Hard cap enforced by the store itself; the HTTP layer uses the same value.\npub const DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES: usize = 32 * 1024 * 1024;\n\n// ---------------- errors ----------------\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StoreError {\n    Vfs(VfsError),\n    NotFound(String),\n    Corrupt { hash: String, detail: String },\n    HashMismatch { declared: String, actual: String },\n    InvalidRootName(String),\n    InvalidHash(String),\n    VersionConflict { name: String, expected: u64, actual: u64 },\n    TooLarge { size: usize, limit: usize },\n    BadMetadata { context: String, detail: String },\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for StoreError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StoreError::Vfs(e) => write!(f, \"{e}\"),\n            StoreError::NotFound(s) => write!(f, \"not found: {s}\"),\n            StoreError::Corrupt { hash, detail } => {\n                write!(f, \"corrupt block {hash}: {detail}\")\n            }\n            StoreError::HashMismatch { declared, actual } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"hash mismatch: declared {declared}, actual sha256 {actual}\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::InvalidRootName(n) => write!(\n                f,\n                \"invalid root name {n:?}: allowed [A-Za-z0-9._-], 1..=128 chars, no leading dot\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::InvalidHash(h) => write!(f, \"invalid sha256 digest: {h}\"),\n            StoreError::VersionConflict {\n                name,\n                expected,\n                actual,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"root {name} version conflict: expected {expected}, current {actual}\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::TooLarge { size, limit } => {\n                write!(f, \"block too large: {size} bytes > limit {limit}\")\n            }\n            StoreError::BadMetadata { context, detail } => {\n                write!(f, \"bad metadata for {context}: {detail}\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StoreError {}\n\nimpl From<VfsError> for StoreError {\n    fn from(e: VfsError) -> Self {\n        StoreError::Vfs(e)\n    }\n}\n\ntype StoreResult<T> = Result<T, StoreError>;\n\npub fn parse_hash(h: &str) -> StoreResult<Sha256> {\n    Sha256::from_hex(h).ok_or_else(|| StoreError::InvalidHash(h.to_string()))\n}\n\n// ---------------- paths & names ----------------\n\nfn validate_root_name(name: &str) -> StoreResult<()> {\n    let ok = name.len() >= 1\n        && name.len() <= 128\n        && !name.starts_with('.')\n        && name\n            .bytes()\n            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b, b'.' | b'_' | b'-'));\n    if ok {\n        Ok(())\n    } else {\n        Err(StoreError::InvalidRootName(name.to_string()))\n    }\n}\n\nfn block_shard(h: &Sha256) -> String {\n    h.to_hex()[..2].to_string()\n}\n\nfn block_blob_rel(h: &Sha256) -> PathBuf {\n    let hex = h.to_hex();\n    PathBuf::from(\"blocks\").join(&hex[..2]).join(&hex[2..])\n}\n\nfn block_refs_rel(h: &Sha256) -> PathBuf {\n    let hex = h.to_hex();\n    PathBuf::from(\"blocks\")\n        .join(&hex[..2])\n        .join(format!(\"{}.refs.json\", &hex[2..]))\n}\n\nfn root_rel(name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    PathBuf::from(\"roots\").join(format!(\"{name}.json\"))\n}\n\n// ---------------- public result types ----------------\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PutOutcome {\n    pub hash: Sha256,\n    /// True when the blob already existed (content de-duplication).\n    pub deduplicated: bool,\n    /// Number of distinct references stored after union with the old sidecar.\n    pub refs_count: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct RootRecord {\n    pub hash: Sha256,\n    pub version: u64,\n    pub updated_at_ms: u64,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct MissingReference {\n    /// Parent digest; `None` when the missing block is a root target.\n    pub parent: Option<String>,\n    pub missing: String,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct GcReport {\n    pub roots_scanned: usize,\n    pub blocks_before: usize,\n    pub blocks_live: usize,\n    pub blocks_removed: usize,\n    pub bytes_removed: u64,\n    pub removed: Vec<String>,\n    pub missing_references: Vec<MissingReference>,\n    pub corrupt_blocks: Vec<String>,\n    pub temp_files_removed: usize,\n    pub warnings: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct StoreStats {\n    pub roots: usize,\n    pub blocks: usize,\n    pub block_bytes: u64,\n}\n\n// ---------------- pin table ----------------\n\n/// Reference-count pins that protect a digest from garbage collection.\n///\n/// Holders: in-flight gets (1 pin for the read duration), uploads (1 pin from\n/// before the existence check until the blob is durable), and GC itself (1 pin\n/// per reachable block for the whole sweep).\npub struct PinTable {\n    counts: Mutex<HashMap<Sha256, usize>>,\n}\n\nimpl PinTable {\n    fn new() -> Self {\n        PinTable {\n            counts: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn pin(&self, h: Sha256) {\n        *self.counts.lock().unwrap().entry(h).or_insert(0) += 1;\n    }\n\n    fn unpin(&self, h: Sha256) {\n        let mut g = self.counts.lock().unwrap();\n        match g.get_mut(&h) {\n            Some(n) if *n > 1 => *n -= 1,\n            Some(_) => {\n                g.remove(&h);\n            }\n            None => debug_assert!(false, \"unpin without pin\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn is_pinned(&self, h: &Sha256) -> bool {\n        self.counts.lock().unwrap().contains_key(h)\n    }\n}\n\n/// RAII pin: released on drop unless `forget()` is called (bulk GC marks).\nstruct Pin<'a> {\n    table: &'a PinTable,\n    hash: Sha256,\n    armed: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> Pin<'a> {\n    fn new(table: &'a PinTable, hash: Sha256) -> Self {\n        table.pin(hash);\n        Pin {\n            table,\n            hash,\n            armed: true,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn disarm(mut self) {\n        self.armed = false;\n        self.table.unpin(self.hash);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for Pin<'_> {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        if self.armed {\n            self.table.unpin(self.hash);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------- store ----------------\n\npub struct Store<V: Vfs = Box<dyn Vfs>> {\n    root: PathBuf,\n    vfs: V,\n    pins: Arc<PinTable>,\n    /// Serializes blob/sidecar publishing so two identical puts cannot race\n    /// each other's temp files.\n    upload: Mutex<()>,\n    /// Root-pointer read/write lock. GC takes a write lock for the full\n    /// mark+sweep so a root switch can never strand a block under deletion.\n    roots_lock: RwLock<()>,\n    max_block_bytes: usize,\n}\n\npub type DynStore = Store<Box<dyn Vfs>>;\n\nimpl DynStore {\n    pub fn open_boxed(data_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, vfs: Box<dyn Vfs>) -> StoreResult<Arc<Self>> {\n        Self::open(data_dir, vfs)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<V: Vfs> Store<V> {\n    pub fn open(data_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, vfs: V) -> StoreResult<Arc<Self>> {\n        let root: PathBuf = data_dir.into();\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root, \"mkdir_data\")?;\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root.join(\"blocks\"), \"mkdir_blocks\")?;\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root.join(\"roots\"), \"mkdir_roots\")?;\n\n        let version_path = root.join(\"VERSION\");\n        match vfs.read(&version_path, \"read_version\") {\n            Ok(bytes) => {\n                if bytes != FORMAT_VERSION_LINE.as_bytes() {\n                    return Err(StoreError::BadMetadata {\n                        context: \"VERSION\".into(),\n                        detail: format!(\"unexpected contents: {:?}\", String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes)),\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => {\n                vfs.write_atomic(&version_path, FORMAT_VERSION_LINE.as_bytes(), \"rename_version\")?;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n        }\n\n        let store = Arc::new(Store {\n            root,\n            vfs,\n            pins: Arc::new(PinTable::new()),\n            upload: Mutex::new(()),\n            roots_lock: RwLock::new(()),\n            max_block_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES,\n        });\n        store.cleanup_temp_files()?;\n        Ok(store)\n    }\n\n    pub fn data_dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.root\n    }\n\n    fn p(&self, rel: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n        self.root.join(rel)\n    }\n\n    /// Remove leftover staging files from interrupted writes (best effort).\n    fn cleanup_temp_files(&self) -> StoreResult<()> {\n        for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&self.p(Path::new(\"roots\")), \"list_roots\")? {\n            if entry.starts_with('.') {\n                let _ = self\n                    .vfs\n                    .remove_file(&self.p(Path::new(\"roots\")).join(&entry), \"cleanup_temp\");\n            }\n        }\n        for shard in self.vfs.list_dir(&self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\")), \"list_blocks\")? {\n            if shard.len() != 2 || !shard.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let shard_path = self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\")).join(&shard);\n            for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&shard_path, \"list_shard\")? {\n                if entry.starts_with('.') {\n                    let _ = self.vfs.remove_file(&shard_path.join(&entry), \"cleanup_temp\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ---------- blocks ----------\n\n    /// Store `data`. If `declared` is given it must match the actual SHA-256.\n    /// `refs` declares outgoing references (union with any prior sidecar);\n    /// references may point at blocks not yet uploaded (forward references).\n    pub fn put_block(\n        &self,\n        data: &[u8],\n        declared: Option<Sha256>,\n        refs: &[Sha256],\n    ) -> StoreResult<PutOutcome> {\n        if data.len() > self.max_block_bytes {\n            return Err(StoreError::TooLarge {\n                size: data.len(),\n                limit: self.max_block_bytes,\n            });\n        }\n        let hash = Sha256::hash(data);\n        if let Some(d) = declared {\n            if d != hash {\n                return Err(StoreError::HashMismatch {\n                    declared: d.to_hex(),\n                    actual: hash.to_hex(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        let _g = self.upload.lock().unwrap();\n        // Pin *before* the existence check: GC cannot remove the blob between\n        // our check and the durable write (sweep holds the same pin lock).\n        let _pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, hash);\n\n        let blob_path = self.p(&block_blob_rel(&hash));\n        let refs_path = self.p(&block_refs_rel(&hash));\n        let existed = self.vfs.exists(&blob_path, \"exists_block\")?;\n\n        if !existed {\n            self.vfs\n                .create_dir_all(blob_path.parent().unwrap(), \"mkdir_shard\")?;\n            self.vfs\n                .write_atomic(&blob_path, data, \"rename_block\")?;\n        }\n\n        let mut all: HashSet<Sha256> =\n            match self.vfs.read(&refs_path, \"read_refs\") {\n                Ok(bytes) => parse_refs_sidecar(&bytes, &hash.to_hex())?.into_iter().collect(),\n                Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => HashSet::new(),\n                Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n            };\n        let before = all.len();\n        all.extend(refs.iter().copied());\n\n        // Rewrite the sidecar whenever refs changed or when writing a fresh\n        // blob that was given refs.\n        if all.len() != before || (!existed && !all.is_empty()) {\n            let doc = build_refs_sidecar(&all);\n            self.vfs\n                .write_atomic(&refs_path, doc.as_bytes(), \"rename_block_refs\")?;\n        }\n\n        Ok(PutOutcome {\n            hash,\n            deduplicated: existed,\n            refs_count: all.len(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Read a block, holding a GC pin for the duration and verifying the\n    /// digest of the bytes on disk.\n    pub fn get_block(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<Vec<u8>> {\n        let _pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, *hash);\n        let path = self.p(&block_blob_rel(hash));\n        let data = match self.vfs.read(&path, \"read_block\") {\n            Ok(d) => d,\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => {\n                return Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\"block {}\", hash.to_hex())))\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n        };\n        // Integrity verification: the digest is the content identity. A\n        // mismatch means bit rot or out-of-band tampering, never \"a different\n        // but acceptable block\".\n        if Sha256::hash(&data) != *hash {\n            return Err(StoreError::Corrupt {\n                hash: hash.to_hex(),\n                detail: \"stored bytes do not hash to their address\".into(),\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(data)\n    }\n\n    pub fn block_exists(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<bool> {\n        Ok(self\n            .vfs\n            .exists(&self.p(&block_blob_rel(hash)), \"exists_block\")?)\n    }\n\n    pub fn block_refs(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<Vec<Sha256>> {\n        match self.vfs.read(&self.p(&block_refs_rel(hash)), \"read_refs\") {\n            Ok(bytes) => parse_refs_sidecar(&bytes, &hash.to_hex()),\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => Ok(Vec::new()),\n            Err(e) => Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn block_info(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<Json> {\n        let present = self.block_exists(hash)?;\n        let refs = self.block_refs(hash)?;\n        let mut obj = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n        obj.insert(\"hash\".into(), Json::str(hash.to_hex()));\n        obj.insert(\"present\".into(), Json::Bool(present));\n        obj.insert(\n            \"refs\".into(),\n            Json::Arr(refs.iter().map(|r| Json::str(r.to_hex())).collect()),\n        );\n        Ok(Json::Obj(obj))\n    }\n\n    // ---------- roots ----------\n\n    /// Publish a root pointer atomically. `expected_version` implements\n    /// optimistic concurrency: the update succeeds only when the on-disk\n    /// version equals it (a missing root counts as version 0).\n    pub fn put_root(\n        &self,\n        name: &str,\n        hash: Sha256,\n        expected_version: Option<u64>,\n    ) -> StoreResult<RootRecord> {\n        validate_root_name(name)?;\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.write().unwrap();\n\n        // The target blob must exist. Pin it until the pointer is published so\n        // GC (which cannot run concurrently — same write lock — but defense in\n        // depth) cannot remove the block between check and publish.\n        let _pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, hash);\n        if !self.vfs.exists(&self.p(&block_blob_rel(&hash)), \"exists_block\")? {\n            return Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\n                \"block {} referenced by new root {name}\",\n                hash.to_hex()\n            )));\n        }\n\n        let path = self.p(&root_rel(name));\n        let current = self.read_root_locked(name)?;\n        let next_version = current.as_ref().map(|r| r.version + 1).unwrap_or(1);\n        if let Some(expected) = expected_version {\n            let actual = current.as_ref().map(|r| r.version).unwrap_or(0);\n            if expected != actual {\n                return Err(StoreError::VersionConflict {\n                    name: name.to_string(),\n                    expected,\n                    actual,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        let rec = RootRecord {\n            hash,\n            version: next_version,\n            updated_at_ms: now_ms(),\n        };\n        let doc = build_root_doc(&rec);\n        // Single atomic publish step. If this call fails (including an\n        // injected fault), no root file is created/modified: the old pointer\n        // stays readable and the new block is simply unreachable.\n        self.vfs.write_atomic(&path, doc.as_bytes(), \"rename_root\")?;\n        Ok(rec)\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_root(&self, name: &str) -> StoreResult<RootRecord> {\n        validate_root_name(name)?;\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.read().unwrap();\n        match self.read_root_locked(name)? {\n            Some(r) => Ok(r),\n            None => Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\"root {name}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn list_roots(&self) -> StoreResult<Vec<(String, RootRecord)>> {\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.read().unwrap();\n        self.list_roots_locked()\n    }\n\n    pub fn delete_root(&self, name: &str) -> StoreResult<bool> {\n        validate_root_name(name)?;\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.write().unwrap();\n        let path = self.p(&root_rel(name));\n        match self.vfs.remove_file(&path, \"delete_root\") {\n            Ok(()) => Ok(true),\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => Ok(false),\n            Err(e) => Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn read_root_locked(&self, name: &str) -> StoreResult<Option<RootRecord>> {\n        let path = self.p(&root_rel(name));\n        match self.vfs.read(&path, \"read_root\") {\n            Ok(bytes) => Ok(Some(parse_root_doc(&bytes, name)?)),\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => Ok(None),\n            Err(e) => Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn list_roots_locked(&self) -> StoreResult<Vec<(String, RootRecord)>> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&self.p(Path::new(\"roots\")), \"list_roots\")? {\n            let Some(name) = entry.strip_suffix(\".json\") else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            if name.starts_with('.') {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if let Ok(Some(rec)) = self.read_root_locked(name) {\n                out.push((name.to_string(), rec));\n            }\n        }\n        out.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n\n    // ---------- GC ----------\n\n    /// Mark all blocks reachable from named roots through reference sidecars,\n    /// then sweep every unpinned blob. root pointer may change during marking or sweeping.\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.write().unwrap();\n\n        let mut report = GcReport::default();\n\n        // ---- mark ----\n        let mut marked: HashSet<Sha256> = HashSet::new();\n        let mut queue: Vec<(Option<Sha256>, Sha256)> = Vec::new(); // (parent, child)\n\n        let roots = self.list_roots_locked()?;\n     Err(e) => {\n                    report.warnings.push(format!(\n                        \"cannot stat {}: {e}\",\n                        hash.to_hex()\n                    ));\n report.corrupt_blocks.push(hash.to_hex());\n                }\n            } else {\n                report\n                    .warnings\n                    .push(format!(\"cannot read {}\", self.block_refs(&hash).unwrap_or_default() {\n                if !marked.contains(&child) {\n                    queue.push((Some(hash), child));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        report.blocks_live = marked.len();\n\n        // ---- sweep ----\n        let blocks_dir = self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\"));\n        let shards = self.vfs.list_dir(&blocks_dir, \"list_blocks\")?;\n ) -> StoreResult<()> {\n        let hex = format!(\"{shard}{rest}\");\n        let hash = match parse_hash(&hex) {\n            Ok(h) => h,\n            Err(_) => {\n                report\n in-flight get or an upload in progress: reachable\n            // or not, it is protected this round.\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let size = self\n            .vfs\n shard in self.vfs.list_dir(&blocks_dir, \"list_blocks\")? {\n            if shard.len() != 2 || !shard.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&blocks_dir.join(&shard), \"list_shard\")? {\n                if entry.len() == 62 && entry.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                    stats.blocks += in bulk after the sweep.\nimpl<'a> Pin<'a> {\n    /// Release ownership of the pin to the caller (pin stays armed in the\n    /// table; caller must unpin it later).\n    fn disarm_and_keep(mut self, _table: &'a PinTable, _hash: Sha256) {\n        self.armed = false;\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------- metadata codecs ----------------\n\nfn build_refs_sidecar(refs: &HashSet<Sha256>) -> String {\n    let mut v: Vec<String> = refs.iter().map(|h| h.to_hex()).collect();\n    v.sort();\n    let arr = Json::Arr(v.into_iter().map(Json::str).collect());\n    let mut obj = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n    obj.insert(\"version\".into(), Json::from_u64(1));\n    obj.insert(\"refs\".into(), arr);\n    Json::Obj(obj).to_compact_string()\n}\n\nfn format!(\"refs of {context_hash}\"),\n            detail: \"missing \\\"refs\\\" array\".into(),\n        }\n    })?;\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    for item in arr {\n        let s = item.as_str().ok_or_else(|| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n            context: format!(\"refs of {context_hash}\"),\n            detail: \"ref entry is not a string\".into(),\n        })?;\n        out.push(parse_hash(s)?);\n    }\n    Ok(out)\n}\n\nfn build_root_doc(rec: &RootRecord) -> String {\n    let mut obj = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n    obj.insert(\"hash\".into(), Json::str(rec.hash.to_hex()));\n    obj.insert(\"version\".into(), Json::from_u64(rec.version));\n    obj.insert(\"updated_at_ms\".into(), Json::from_u64(rec.updated_at_ms));\n    Json::Obj(obj).to_compact_string()\n}\n\nfn parse_root_doc(bytes: &[u8], name: &str) -> StoreResult<RootRecord> {\n    let text = std::str::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n        context: format!(\"root {name}\"),\n        detail: \"not utf-8\".into(),\n    })?;\n    let doc = crate::json::parse(text).map_err(|e| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n        context: format!(\"root {name}\"),\n        detail: e.to_string(),\n    })?;\n    let hash = parse_hash(\n        doc.get(\"hash\")\n            .and_then(Json::as_str)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n updated_at_ms = doc\n        .get(\"updated_at_ms\")\n        .and_then(Json::as_u64)\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n    Ok(RootRecord {\n        hash,\n        version,\n        updated_at_ms,\n    })\n}\n\nfn now_ms() -> u64 {\n    std::time::SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_millis() as u64)\n File-backed content-addressable block store.\n//!\n//! ## Disk format (version 1)\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! <data-dir>/\n//!   VERSION                       # contains \"cas-repo v1\\n\"\n//!   blocks/\n//!     <aa>/                       # first byte of the digest, 256 shards\n//!       <rest-62-hex>             # immutable blob: exact block bytes\n//!       <rest-62-hex>.refs.json   # sidecar: {\"version\":1,\"refs\":[\"<sha256>\", ...]}\n//!       .<...>.tmp-<rand>         # staging files (atomic rename source)\n//!   roots/\n//!     <name>.json                 # {\"hash\":\"<sha256>\",\"version\":N,\"updated_at_ms\":T}\n//!     .<name>.json.tmp-<rand>     # staging files\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Invariants:\n//! * Blob bytes always hash to their path digest. Hash is verified on read and\n//!   during GC marking; it is an integrity check only, never an access token.\n//! * Blobs are immutable: a `put` of an existing digest never rewrites the\n//!   blob, only unions the declared reference set.\n//! * A root pointer appears via one temp-file + fsync + rename step, so root\n//!   updates are atomic: readers see either the old or the new version.\n//!\n//! ## Synchronization boundary\n//!\n//! One store object owns one data directory (single process). Internally:\n//! * `upload` serializes puts of the *same* staging paths;\n//! * a `RwLock` guards root-pointer changes against GC;\n//! * the pin table counts in-flight readers and GC-live blocks. Sweep checks\n//!   the pin count and deletes while holding the pin lock, closing the\n//!   reader/GC and uploader/GC windows.\n\nuse std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, RwLock};\n\nuse crate::hash::Sha256;\nuse crate::json::Json;\nuse crate::vfs::{VfsError, VfsResult, Vfs};\n\nconst FORMAT_VERSION_LINE: &str = \"cas-repo v1\\n\";\n/// Hard cap enforced by the store itself; the HTTP layer uses the same value.\npub const DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES: usize = 32 * 1024 * 1024;\n\n// ---------------- errors ----------------\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StoreError {\n    Vfs(VfsError),\n    NotFound(String),\n    Corrupt { hash: String, detail: String },\n    HashMismatch { declared: String, actual: String },\n    InvalidRootName(String),\n    InvalidHash(String),\n    VersionConflict { name: String, expected: u64, actual: u64 },\n    TooLarge { size: usize, limit: usize },\n    BadMetadata { context: String, detail: String },\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for StoreError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StoreError::Vfs(e) => write!(f, \"{e}\"),\n            StoreError::NotFound(s) => write!(f, \"not found: {s}\"),\n            StoreError::Corrupt { hash, detail } => {\n                write!(f, \"corrupt block {hash}: {detail}\")\n            }\n            StoreError::HashMismatch { declared, actual } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"hash mismatch: declared {declared}, actual sha256 {actual}\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::InvalidRootName(n) => write!(\n                f,\n                \"invalid root name {n:?}: allowed [A-Za-z0-9._-], 1..=128 chars, no leading dot\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::InvalidHash(h) => write!(f, \"invalid sha256 digest: {h}\"),\n            StoreError::VersionConflict {\n                name,\n                expected,\n                actual,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"root {name} version conflict: expected {expected}, current {actual}\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::TooLarge { size, limit } => {\n                write!(f, \"block too large: {size} bytes > limit {limit}\")\n            }\n            StoreError::BadMetadata { context, detail } => {\n                write!(f, \"bad metadata for {context}: {detail}\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StoreError {}\n\nimpl From<VfsError> for StoreError {\n    fn from(e: VfsError) -> Self {\n        StoreError::Vfs(e)\n    }\n}\n\ntype StoreResult<T> = Result<T, StoreError>;\n\npub fn parse_hash(h: &str) -> StoreResult<Sha256> {\n    Sha256::from_hex(h).ok_or_else(|| StoreError::InvalidHash(h.to_string()))\n}\n\n// ---------------- paths & names ----------------\n\nfn validate_root_name(name: &str) -> StoreResult<()> {\n    let ok = name.len() >= 1\n        && name.len() <= 128\n        && !name.starts_with('.')\n        && name\n            .bytes()\n            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b, b'.' | b'_' | b'-'));\n    if ok {\n        Ok(())\n    } else {\n        Err(StoreError::InvalidRootName(name.to_string()))\n    }\n}\n\nfn block_shard(h: &Sha256) -> String {\n    h.to_hex()[..2].to_string()\n}\n\nfn block_blob_rel(h: &Sha256) -> PathBuf {\n    let hex = h.to_hex();\n    PathBuf::from(\"blocks\").join(&hex[..2]).join(&hex[2..])\n}\n\nfn block_refs_rel(h: &Sha256) -> PathBuf {\n    let hex = h.to_hex();\n    PathBuf::from(\"blocks\")\n        .join(&hex[..2])\n        .join(format!(\"{}.refs.json\", &hex[2..]))\n}\n\nfn root_rel(name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    PathBuf::from(\"roots\").join(format!(\"{name}.json\"))\n}\n\n// ---------------- public result types ----------------\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PutOutcome {\n    pub hash: Sha256,\n    /// True when the blob already existed (content de-duplication).\n    pub deduplicated: bool,\n    /// Number of distinct references stored after union with the old sidecar.\n    pub refs_count: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct RootRecord {\n    pub hash: Sha256,\n    pub version: u64,\n    pub updated_at_ms: u64,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct MissingReference {\n    /// Parent digest; `None` when the missing block is a root target.\n    pub parent: Option<String>,\n    pub missing: String,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct GcReport {\n    pub roots_scanned: usize,\n    pub blocks_before: usize,\n    pub blocks_live: usize,\n    pub blocks_removed: usize,\n    pub bytes_removed: u64,\n    pub removed: Vec<String>,\n    pub missing_references: Vec<MissingReference>,\n    pub corrupt_blocks: Vec<String>,\n    pub temp_files_removed: usize,\n    pub warnings: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct StoreStats {\n    pub roots: usize,\n    pub blocks: usize,\n    pub block_bytes: u64,\n}\n\n// ---------------- pin table ----------------\n\n/// Reference-count pins that protect a digest from garbage collection.\n///\n/// Holders: in-flight gets (1 pin for the read duration), uploads (1 pin from\n/// before the existence check until the blob is durable), and GC itself (1 pin\n/// per reachable block for the whole sweep).\npub struct PinTable {\n    counts: Mutex<HashMap<Sha256, usize>>,\n}\n\nimpl PinTable {\n    fn new() -> Self {\n        PinTable {\n            counts: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn pin(&self, h: Sha256) {\n        *self.counts.lock().unwrap().entry(h).or_insert(0) += 1;\n    }\n\n    fn unpin(&self, h: Sha256) {\n        let mut g = self.counts.lock().unwrap();\n        match g.get_mut(&h) {\n            Some(n) if *n > 1 => *n -= 1,\n            Some(_) => {\n                g.remove(&h);\n            }\n            None => debug_assert!(false, \"unpin without pin\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn is_pinned(&self, h: &Sha256) -> bool {\n        self.counts.lock().unwrap().contains_key(h)\n    }\n}\n\n/// RAII pin: released on drop unless `forget()` is called (bulk GC marks).\nstruct Pin<'a> {\n    table: &'a PinTable,\n    hash: Sha256,\n    armed: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> Pin<'a> {\n    fn new(table: &'a PinTable, hash: Sha256) -> Self {\n        table.pin(hash);\n        Pin {\n            table,\n            hash,\n            armed: true,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn disarm(mut self) {\n        self.armed = false;\n        self.table.unpin(self.hash);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for Pin<'_> {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        if self.armed {\n            self.table.unpin(self.hash);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------- store ----------------\n\npub struct Store<V: Vfs = Box<dyn Vfs>> {\n    root: PathBuf,\n    vfs: V,\n    pins: Arc<PinTable>,\n    /// Serializes blob/sidecar publishing so two identical puts cannot race\n    /// each other's temp files.\n    upload: Mutex<()>,\n    /// Root-pointer read/write lock. GC takes a write lock for the full\n    /// mark+sweep so a root switch can never strand a block under deletion.\n    roots_lock: RwLock<()>,\n    max_block_bytes: usize,\n}\n\npub type DynStore = Store<Box<dyn Vfs>>;\n\nimpl DynStore {\n    pub fn open_boxed(data_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, vfs: Box<dyn Vfs>) -> StoreResult<Arc<Self>> {\n        Self::open(data_dir, vfs)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<V: Vfs> Store<V> {\n    pub fn open(data_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, vfs: V) -> StoreResult<Arc<Self>> {\n        let root: PathBuf = data_dir.into();\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root, \"mkdir_data\")?;\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root.join(\"blocks\"), \"mkdir_blocks\")?;\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root.join(\"roots\"), \"mkdir_roots\")?;\n\n        let version_path = root.join(\"VERSION\");\n        match vfs.read(&version_path, \"read_version\") {\n            Ok(bytes) => {\n                if bytes != FORMAT_VERSION_LINE.as_bytes() {\n                    return Err(StoreError::BadMetadata {\n                        context: \"VERSION\".into(),\n                        detail: format!(\"unexpected contents: {:?}\", String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes)),\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => {\n                vfs.write_atomic(&version_path, FORMAT_VERSION_LINE.as_bytes(), \"rename_version\")?;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n        }\n\n        let store = Arc::new(Store {\n            root,\n            vfs,\n            pins: Arc::new(PinTable::new()),\n            upload: Mutex::new(()),\n            roots_lock: RwLock::new(()),\n            max_block_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES,\n        });\n        store.cleanup_temp_files()?;\n        Ok(store)\n    }\n\n    pub fn data_dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.root\n    }\n\n    fn p(&self, rel: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n        self.root.join(rel)\n    }\n\n    /// Remove leftover staging files from interrupted writes (best effort).\n    fn cleanup_temp_files(&self) -> StoreResult<()> {\n        for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&self.p(Path::new(\"roots\")), \"list_roots\")? {\n            if entry.starts_with('.') {\n                let _ = self\n                    .vfs\n                    .remove_file(&self.p(Path::new(\"roots\")).join(&entry), \"cleanup_temp\");\n            }\n        }\n        for shard in self.vfs.list_dir(&self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\")), \"list_blocks\")? {\n            if shard.len() != 2 || !shard.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let shard_path = self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\")).join(&shard);\n            for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&shard_path, \"list_shard\")? {\n                if entry.starts_with('.') {\n                    let _ = self.vfs.remove_file(&shard_path.join(&entry), \"cleanup_temp\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ---------- blocks ----------\n\n    /// Store `data`. If `declared` is given it must match the actual SHA-256.\n    /// `refs` declares outgoing references (union with any prior sidecar);\n    /// references may point at blocks not yet uploaded (forward references).\n    pub fn put_block(\n        &self,\n        data: &[u8],\n        declared: Option<Sha256>,\n        refs: &[Sha256],\n    ) -> StoreResult<PutOutcome> {\n        if data.len() > self.max_block_bytes {\n            return Err(StoreError::TooLarge {\n                size: data.len(),\n                limit: self.max_block_bytes,\n            });\n        }\n        let hash = Sha256::hash(data);\n        if let Some(d) = declared {\n            if d != hash {\n                return Err(StoreError::HashMismatch {\n                    declared: d.to_hex(),\n                    actual: hash.to_hex(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        let _g = self.upload.lock().unwrap();\n        // Pin *before* the existence check: GC cannot remove the blob between\n        // our check and the durable write (sweep holds the same pin lock).\n        let _pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, hash);\n\n        let blob_path = self.p(&block_blob_rel(&hash));\n        let refs_path = self.p(&block_refs_rel(&hash));\n        let existed = self.vfs.exists(&blob_path, \"exists_block\")?;\n\n        if !existed {\n            self.vfs\n                .create_dir_all(blob_path.parent().unwrap(), \"mkdir_shard\")?;\n            self.vfs\n                .write_atomic(&blob_path, data, \"rename_block\")?;\n        }\n\n        let mut all: HashSet<Sha256> =\n            match self.vfs.read(&refs_path, \"read_refs\") {\n                Ok(bytes) => parse_refs_sidecar(&bytes, &hash.to_hex())?.into_iter().collect(),\n                Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => HashSet::new(),\n                Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n            };\n        let before = all.len();\n        all.extend(refs.iter().copied());\n\n        // Rewrite the sidecar whenever refs changed or when writing a fresh\n        // blob that was given refs.\n        if all.len() != before || (!existed && !all.is_empty()) {\n            let doc = build_refs_sidecar(&all);\n            self.vfs\n                .write_atomic(&refs_path, doc.as_bytes(), \"rename_block_refs\")?;\n        }\n\n        Ok(PutOutcome {\n            hash,\n            deduplicated: existed,\n            refs_count: all.len(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Read a block, holding a GC pin for the duration and verifying the\n    /// digest of the bytes on disk.\n    pub fn get_block(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<Vec<u8>> {\n        let _pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, *hash);\n        let path = self.p(&block_blob_rel(hash));\n        let data = match self.vfs.read(&path, \"read_block\") {\n            Ok(d) => d,\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => {\n                return Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\"block {}\", hash.to_hex())))\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n        };\n        // Integrity verification: the digest is the content identity. A\n        // mismatch means bit rot or out-of-band tampering, never \"a different\n        // but acceptable block\".\n        if Sha256::hash(&data) != *hash {\n            return Err(StoreError::Corrupt {\n                hash: hash.to_hex(),\n                detail: \"stored bytes do not hash to their address\".into(),\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(data)\n    }\n\n    pub fn block_exists(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<bool> {\n        Ok(self\n            .vfs\n            .exists(&self.p(&block_blob_rel(hash)), \"exists_block\")?)\n    }\n\n    pub fn block_refs(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<Vec<Sha256>> {\n        match self.vfs.read(&self.p(&block_refs_rel(hash)), \"read_refs\") {\n            Ok(bytes) => parse_refs_sidecar(&bytes, &hash.to_hex()),\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => Ok(Vec::new()),\n            Err(e) => Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn block_info(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<Json> {\n        let present = self.block_exists(hash)?;\n        let refs = self.block_refs(hash)?;\n        let mut obj = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n        obj.insert(\"hash\".into(), Json::str(hash.to_hex()));\n        obj.insert(\"present\".into(), Json::Bool(present));\n        obj.insert(\n            \"refs\".into(),\n            Json::Arr(refs.iter().map(|r| Json::str(r.to_hex())).collect()),\n        );\n        Ok(Json::Obj(obj))\n    }\n\n    // ---------- roots ----------\n\n    /// Publish a root pointer atomically. `expected_version` implements\n    /// optimistic concurrency: the update succeeds only when the on-disk\n    /// version equals it (a missing root counts as version 0).\n    pub fn put_root(\n        &self,\n        name: &str,\n        hash: Sha256,\n        expected_version: Option<u64>,\n    ) -> StoreResult<RootRecord> {\n        validate_root_name(name)?;\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.write().unwrap();\n\n        // The target blob must exist. Pin it until the pointer is published so\n        // GC (which cannot run concurrently — same write lock — but defense in\n        // depth) cannot remove the block between check and publish.\n        let _pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, hash);\n        if !self.vfs.exists(&self.p(&block_blob_rel(&hash)), \"exists_block\")? {\n            return Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\n                \"block {} referenced by new root {name}\",\n                hash.to_hex()\n            )));\n        }\n\n        let path = self.p(&root_rel(name));\n        let current = self.read_root_locked(name)?;\n        let next_version = current.as_ref().map(|r| r.version + 1).unwrap_or(1);\n        if let Some(expected) = expected_version {\n            let actual = current.as_ref().map(|r| r.version).unwrap_or(0);\n            if expected != actual {\n                return Err(StoreError::VersionConflict {\n                    name: name.to_string(),\n                    expected,\n                    actual,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        let rec = RootRecord {\n            hash,\n            version: next_version,\n            updated_at_ms: now_ms(),\n        };\n        let doc = build_root_doc(&rec);\n        // Single atomic publish step. If this call fails (including an\n        // injected fault), no root file is created/modified: the old pointer\n        // stays readable and the new block is simply unreachable.\n        self.vfs.write_atomic(&path, doc.as_bytes(), \"rename_root\")?;\n        Ok(rec)\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_root(&self, name: &str) -> StoreResult<RootRecord> {\n        validate_root_name(name)?;\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.read().unwrap();\n        match self.read_root_locked(name)? {\n            Some(r) => Ok(r),\n            None => Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\"root {name}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn list_roots(&self) -> StoreResult<Vec<(String, RootRecord)>> {\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.read().unwrap();\n        self.list_roots_locked()\n    }\n\n    pub fn delete_root(&self, name: &str) -> StoreResult<bool> {\n        validate_root_name(name)?;\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.write().unwrap();\n        let path = self.p(&root_rel(name));\n        match self.vfs.remove_file(&path, \"delete_root\") {\n            Ok(()) => Ok(true),\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => Ok(false),\n            Err(e) => Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn read_root_locked(&self, name: &str) -> StoreResult<Option<RootRecord>> {\n        let path = self.p(&root_rel(name));\n        match self.vfs.read(&path, \"read_root\") {\n            Ok(bytes) => Ok(Some(parse_root_doc(&bytes, name)?)),\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => Ok(None),\n            Err(e) => Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn list_roots_locked(&self) -> StoreResult<Vec<(String, RootRecord)>> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&self.p(Path::new(\"roots\")), \"list_roots\")? {\n            let Some(name) = entry.strip_suffix(\".json\") else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            if name.starts_with('.') {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if let Ok(Some(rec)) = self.read_root_locked(name) {\n                out.push((name.to_string(), rec));\n            }\n        }\n        out.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n\n    // ---------- GC ----------\n\n    /// Mark all blocks reachable from named roots through reference sidecars,\n    /// then sweep every unpinned blob. Root switches are blocked for the whole\n    /// operation; gets/uploads continue to work and their pins protect blocks.\n    pub fn gc(&self) -> StoreResult<GcReport> {\n        // Write lock: no root pointer may change during marking or sweeping.\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.write().unwrap();\n\n        let mut report = GcReport::default();\n\n        // ---- mark ----\n        let mut marked: HashSet<Sha256> = HashSet::new();\n        let mut queue: Vec<(Option<Sha256>, Sha256)> = Vec::new(); // (parent, child)\n\n        let roots = self.list_roots_locked()?;\n        report.roots_scanned = roots.len();\n        for (name, rec) in roots {\n            queue.push((None, rec.hash));\n            let _ = name;\n        }\n\n        while let Some((parent, hash)) = queue.pop() {\n            if marked.contains(&hash) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            // Pin immediately; un-pinned only after the sweep finishes.\n            let pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, hash);\n            let blob = self.p(&block_blob_rel(&hash));\n            let exists = match self.vfs.exists(&blob, \"exists_block\") {\n                Ok(b) => b,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    report.warnings.push(format!(\n                        \"cannot stat {}: {e}\",\n                        hash.to_hex()\n                    ));\n                    pin.disarm();\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n            if !exists {\n                report.missing_references.push(MissingReference {\n                    parent: parent.map(|p| p.to_hex()),\n                    missing: hash.to_hex(),\n                });\n                pin.disarm();\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Verify integrity of every reachable blob.\n            if let Ok(bytes) = self.vfs.read(&blob, \"read_block\") {\n                if Sha256::hash(&bytes) != hash {\n                    report.corrupt_blocks.push(hash.to_hex());\n                }\n            } else {\n                report\n                    .warnings\n                    .push(format!(\"cannot read {}\", hash.to_hex()));\n            }\n\n            marked.insert(hash);\n            pin.disarm_and_keep(&self.pins, hash); // bulk-unpin after sweep\n\n            for child in self.block_refs(&hash).unwrap_or_default() {\n                if !marked.contains(&child) {\n                    queue.push((Some(hash), child));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        report.blocks_live = marked.len();\n\n        // ---- sweep ----\n        let blocks_dir = self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\"));\n        let shards = self.vfs.list_dir(&blocks_dir, \"list_blocks\")?;\n        for shard in shards {\n            if shard.len() != 2 || !shard.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let shard_path = blocks_dir.join(&shard);\n            for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&shard_path, \"list_shard\")? {\n                if entry.starts_with('.') {\n                    // Stale staging file from a crashed/interrupted write.\n                    if self\n                        .vfs\n                        .remove_file(&shard_path.join(&entry), \"remove_temp\")\n                        .is_ok()\n                    {\n                        report.temp_files_removed += 1;\n                    }\n                    continue;\n                }\n                let Some(rest) = entry.strip_suffix(\".refs.json\") else {\n                    // Blob name must be exactly 62 hex chars.\n                    if entry.len() != 62 || !entry.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                        report\n                            .warnings\n                            .push(format!(\"ignoring unexpected file blocks/{shard}/{entry}\"));\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    self.sweep_blob(&shard, &entry, &marked, &mut report)?;\n                    continue;\n                };\n                if rest.len() != 62 || !rest.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                    report\n                        .warnings\n                        .push(format!(\"ignoring unexpected file blocks/{shard}/{entry}\"));\n                }\n                // Sidecars are removed together with their blob in sweep_blob.\n            }\n        }\n\n        report.blocks_before = report.blocks_live + report.blocks_removed;\n\n        // Release the bulk mark pins.\n        for h in &marked {\n            self.pins.unpin(*h);\n        }\n        Ok(report)\n    }\n\n    /// Remove one unreachable blob (and its sidecar). The pin-table lock is\n    /// held across the actual unlink: a concurrent reader/uploader must either\n    /// have its pin visible (skip deletion) or pin *after* the unlink\n    /// completed (and then observe \"not found\" / re-create the blob).\n    fn sweep_blob(\n        &self,\n        shard: &str,\n        rest: &str,\n        marked: &HashSet<Sha256>,\n        report: &mut GcReport,\n    ) -> StoreResult<()> {\n        let hex = format!(\"{shard}{rest}\");\n        let hash = match parse_hash(&hex) {\n            Ok(h) => h,\n            Err(_) => {\n                report\n                    .warnings\n                    .push(format!(\"ignoring non-hash blob blocks/{shard}/{rest}\"));\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        };\n        if marked.contains(&hash) {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let blob_path = self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\")).join(shard).join(rest);\n        let refs_path = self\n            .p(Path::new(\"blocks\"))\n            .join(shard)\n            .join(format!(\"{rest}.refs.json\"));\n\n        let mut counts = self.pins.counts.lock().unwrap();\n        if counts.contains_key(&hash) {\n            // Pinned by an in-flight get or an upload in progress: reachable\n            // or not, it is protected this round.\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let size = self\n            .vfs\n            .read(&blob_path, \"read_block\")\n            .map(|b| b.len() as u64)\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n        self.vfs.remove_file(&blob_path, \"remove_block\")?;\n        if let Err(e) = self.vfs.remove_file(&refs_path, \"remove_refs\") {\n            if !e.is_not_found() {\n                return Err(e.into());\n            }\n        }\n        drop(counts);\n        report.blocks_removed += 1;\n        report.bytes_removed += size;\n        report.removed.push(hex);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ---------- stats ----------\n\n    pub fn stats(&self) -> StoreResult<StoreStats> {\n        let mut stats = StoreStats::default();\n        stats.roots = self.list_roots_locked()?.len();\n        let blocks_dir = self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\"));\n        for shard in self.vfs.list_dir(&blocks_dir, \"list_blocks\")? {\n            if shard.len() != 2 || !shard.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&blocks_dir.join(&shard), \"list_shard\")? {\n                if entry.len() == 62 && entry.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                    stats.blocks += 1;\n                    if let Ok(bytes) = self\n                        .vfs\n                        .read(&blocks_dir.join(&shard).join(&entry), \"read_block\")\n                    {\n                        stats.block_bytes += bytes.len() as u64;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(stats)\n    }\n}\n\n// RAII helper: GC marks a pin that it releases in bulk after the sweep.\nimpl<'a> Pin<'a> {\n    /// Release ownership of the pin to the caller (pin stays armed in the\n    /// table; caller must unpin it later).\n    fn disarm_and_keep(mut self, _table: &'a PinTable, _hash: Sha256) {\n        self.armed = false;\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------- metadata codecs ----------------\n\nfn build_refs_sidecar(refs: &HashSet<Sha256>) -> String {\n    let mut v: Vec<String> = refs.iter().map(|h| h.to_hex()).collect();\n    v.sort();\n    let arr = Json::Arr(v.into_iter().map(Json::str).collect());\n    let mut obj = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n    obj.insert(\"version\".into(), Json::from_u64(1));\n    obj.insert(\"refs\".into(), arr);\n    Json::Obj(obj).to_compact_string()\n}\n\nfn parse_refs_sidecar(bytes: &[u8], context_hash: &str) -> StoreResult<Vec<Sha256>> {\n    let text = std::str::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n        context: format!(\"refs of {context_hash}\"),\n        detail: \"not utf-8\".into(),\n    })?;\n    let doc = crate::json::parse(text).map_err(|e| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n        context: format!(\"refs of {context_hash}\"),\n        detail: e.to_string(),\n    })?;\n    let arr = doc.get(\"refs\").and_then(Json::as_array).ok_or_else(|| {\n        StoreError::BadMetadata {\n            context: format!(\"refs of {context_hash}\"),\n            detail: \"missing \\\"refs\\\" array\".into(),\n        }\n    })?;\n    let mut out = Vec::new();\n    for item in arr {\n        let s = item.as_str().ok_or_else(|| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n            context: format!(\"refs of {context_hash}\"),\n            detail: \"ref entry is not a string\".into(),\n        })?;\n        out.push(parse_hash(s)?);\n    }\n    Ok(out)\n}\n\nfn build_root_doc(rec: &RootRecord) -> String {\n    let mut obj = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n    obj.insert(\"hash\".into(), Json::str(rec.hash.to_hex()));\n    obj.insert(\"version\".into(), Json::from_u64(rec.version));\n    obj.insert(\"updated_at_ms\".into(), Json::from_u64(rec.updated_at_ms));\n    Json::Obj(obj).to_compact_string()\n}\n\nfn parse_root_doc(bytes: &[u8], name: &str) -> StoreResult<RootRecord> {\n    let text = std::str::from_utf8(bytes).map_err(|_| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n        context: format!(\"root {name}\"),\n        detail: \"not utf-8\".into(),\n    })?;\n    let doc = crate::json::parse(text).map_err(|e| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n        context: format!(\"root {name}\"),\n        detail: e.to_string(),\n    })?;\n    let hash = parse_hash(\n        doc.get(\"hash\")\n            .and_then(Json::as_str)\n            .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n                context: format!(\"root {name}\"),\n                detail: \"missing hash\".into(),\n            })?,\n    )?;\n    let version = doc\n        .get(\"version\")\n        .and_then(Json::as_u64)\n        .ok_or_else(|| StoreError::BadMetadata {\n            context: format!(\"root {name}\"),\n            detail: \"missing version\".into(),\n        })?;\n    let updated_at_ms = doc\n        .get(\"updated_at_ms\")\n        .and_then(Json::as_u64)\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n    Ok(RootRecord {\n        hash,\n        version,\n        updated_at_ms,\n    })\n}\n\nfn now_ms() -> u64 {\n    std::time::SystemTime::now()\n        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n        .map(|d| d.as_millis() as u64)\n
