File-backed content-addressable block store.\n//!\n//! ## Disk format (version 1)\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! <data-dir>/\n//!   VERSION                       # contains \"cas-repo v1\\n\"\n//!   blocks/\n//!     <aa>/                       # first byte of the digest, 256 shards\n//!       <rest-62-hex>             # immutable blob: exact block bytes\n//!       <rest-62-hex>.refs.json   # sidecar: {\"version\":1,\"refs\":[\"<sha256>\", ...]}\n//!       .<...>.tmp-<rand>         # staging files (atomic rename source)\n//!   roots/\n//!     <name>.json                 # {\"hash\":\"<sha256>\",\"version\":N,\"updated_at_ms\":T}\n//!     .<name>.json.tmp-<rand>     # staging files\n//! ```\n//!\n//! Invariants:\n//! * Blob bytes always hash to their path digest. Hash is verified on read and\n//!   during GC marking; it is an integrity check only, never an access token.\n//! * Blobs are immutable: a `put` of an existing digest never rewrites the\n//!   blob, only unions the declared reference set.\n//! * A root pointer appears via one temp-file + fsync + rename step, so root\n//!   updates are atomic: readers see either the old or the new version.\n//!\n//! ## Synchronization boundary\n//!\n//! One store object owns one data directory (single process). Internally:\n//! * `upload` serializes puts of the *same* staging paths;\n//! * a `RwLock` guards root-pointer changes against GC;\n//! * the pin table counts in-flight readers and GC-live blocks. Sweep checks\n//!   the pin count and deletes while holding the pin lock, closing the\n//!   reader/GC and uploader/GC windows.\n\nuse std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, RwLock};\n\nuse crate::hash::Sha256;\nuse crate::json::Json;\nuse crate::vfs::{VfsError, VfsResult, Vfs};\n\nconst FORMAT_VERSION_LINE: &str = \"cas-repo v1\\n\";\n/// Hard cap enforced by the store itself; the HTTP layer uses the same value.\npub const DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES: usize = 32 * 1024 * 1024;\n\n// ---------------- errors ----------------\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StoreError {\n    Vfs(VfsError),\n    NotFound(String),\n    Corrupt { hash: String, detail: String },\n    HashMismatch { declared: String, actual: String },\n    InvalidRootName(String),\n    InvalidHash(String),\n    VersionConflict { name: String, expected: u64, actual: u64 },\n    TooLarge { size: usize, limit: usize },\n    BadMetadata { context: String, detail: String },\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for StoreError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StoreError::Vfs(e) => write!(f, \"{e}\"),\n            StoreError::NotFound(s) => write!(f, \"not found: {s}\"),\n            StoreError::Corrupt { hash, detail } => {\n                write!(f, \"corrupt block {hash}: {detail}\")\n            }\n            StoreError::HashMismatch { declared, actual } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"hash mismatch: declared {declared}, actual sha256 {actual}\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::InvalidRootName(n) => write!(\n                f,\n                \"invalid root name {n:?}: allowed [A-Za-z0-9._-], 1..=128 chars, no leading dot\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::InvalidHash(h) => write!(f, \"invalid sha256 digest: {h}\"),\n            StoreError::VersionConflict {\n                name,\n                expected,\n                actual,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"root {name} version conflict: expected {expected}, current {actual}\"\n            ),\n            StoreError::TooLarge { size, limit } => {\n                write!(f, \"block too large: {size} bytes > limit {limit}\")\n            }\n            StoreError::BadMetadata { context, detail } => {\n                write!(f, \"bad metadata for {context}: {detail}\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StoreError {}\n\nimpl From<VfsError> for StoreError {\n    fn from(e: VfsError) -> Self {\n        StoreError::Vfs(e)\n    }\n}\n\ntype StoreResult<T> = Result<T, StoreError>;\n\npub fn parse_hash(h: &str) -> StoreResult<Sha256> {\n    Sha256::from_hex(h).ok_or_else(|| StoreError::InvalidHash(h.to_string()))\n}\n\n// ---------------- paths & names ----------------\n\nfn validate_root_name(name: &str) -> StoreResult<()> {\n    let ok = name.len() >= 1\n        && name.len() <= 128\n        && !name.starts_with('.')\n        && name\n            .bytes()\n            .all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b, b'.' | b'_' | b'-'));\n    if ok {\n        Ok(())\n    } else {\n        Err(StoreError::InvalidRootName(name.to_string()))\n    }\n}\n\nfn block_shard(h: &Sha256) -> String {\n    h.to_hex()[..2].to_string()\n}\n\nfn block_blob_rel(h: &Sha256) -> PathBuf {\n    let hex = h.to_hex();\n    PathBuf::from(\"blocks\").join(&hex[..2]).join(&hex[2..])\n}\n\nfn block_refs_rel(h: &Sha256) -> PathBuf {\n    let hex = h.to_hex();\n    PathBuf::from(\"blocks\")\n        .join(&hex[..2])\n        .join(format!(\"{}.refs.json\", &hex[2..]))\n}\n\nfn root_rel(name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    PathBuf::from(\"roots\").join(format!(\"{name}.json\"))\n}\n\n// ---------------- public result types ----------------\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct PutOutcome {\n    pub hash: Sha256,\n    /// True when the blob already existed (content de-duplication).\n    pub deduplicated: bool,\n    /// Number of distinct references stored after union with the old sidecar.\n    pub refs_count: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct RootRecord {\n    pub hash: Sha256,\n    pub version: u64,\n    pub updated_at_ms: u64,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct MissingReference {\n    /// Parent digest; `None` when the missing block is a root target.\n    pub parent: Option<String>,\n    pub missing: String,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct GcReport {\n    pub roots_scanned: usize,\n    pub blocks_before: usize,\n    pub blocks_live: usize,\n    pub blocks_removed: usize,\n    pub bytes_removed: u64,\n    pub removed: Vec<String>,\n    pub missing_references: Vec<MissingReference>,\n    pub corrupt_blocks: Vec<String>,\n    pub temp_files_removed: usize,\n    pub warnings: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct StoreStats {\n    pub roots: usize,\n    pub blocks: usize,\n    pub block_bytes: u64,\n}\n\n// ---------------- pin table ----------------\n\n/// Reference-count pins that protect a digest from garbage collection.\n///\n/// Holders: in-flight gets (1 pin for the read duration), uploads (1 pin from\n/// before the existence check until the blob is durable), and GC itself (1 pin\n/// per reachable block for the whole sweep).\npub struct PinTable {\n    counts: Mutex<HashMap<Sha256, usize>>,\n}\n\nimpl PinTable {\n    fn new() -> Self {\n        PinTable {\n            counts: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn pin(&self, h: Sha256) {\n        *self.counts.lock().unwrap().entry(h).or_insert(0) += 1;\n    }\n\n    fn unpin(&self, h: Sha256) {\n        let mut g = self.counts.lock().unwrap();\n        match g.get_mut(&h) {\n            Some(n) if *n > 1 => *n -= 1,\n            Some(_) => {\n                g.remove(&h);\n            }\n            None => debug_assert!(false, \"unpin without pin\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn is_pinned(&self, h: &Sha256) -> bool {\n        self.counts.lock().unwrap().contains_key(h)\n    }\n}\n\n/// RAII pin: released on drop unless `forget()` is called (bulk GC marks).\nstruct Pin<'a> {\n    table: &'a PinTable,\n    hash: Sha256,\n    armed: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> Pin<'a> {\n    fn new(table: &'a PinTable, hash: Sha256) -> Self {\n        table.pin(hash);\n        Pin {\n            table,\n            hash,\n            armed: true,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn disarm(mut self) {\n        self.armed = false;\n        self.table.unpin(self.hash);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for Pin<'_> {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        if self.armed {\n            self.table.unpin(self.hash);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------- store ----------------\n\npub struct Store<V: Vfs = Box<dyn Vfs>> {\n    root: PathBuf,\n    vfs: V,\n    pins: Arc<PinTable>,\n    /// Serializes blob/sidecar publishing so two identical puts cannot race\n    /// each other's temp files.\n    upload: Mutex<()>,\n    /// Root-pointer read/write lock. GC takes a write lock for the full\n    /// mark+sweep so a root switch can never strand a block under deletion.\n    roots_lock: RwLock<()>,\n    max_block_bytes: usize,\n}\n\npub type DynStore = Store<Box<dyn Vfs>>;\n\nimpl DynStore {\n    pub fn open_boxed(data_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, vfs: Box<dyn Vfs>) -> StoreResult<Arc<Self>> {\n        Self::open(data_dir, vfs)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<V: Vfs> Store<V> {\n    pub fn open(data_dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, vfs: V) -> StoreResult<Arc<Self>> {\n        let root: PathBuf = data_dir.into();\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root, \"mkdir_data\")?;\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root.join(\"blocks\"), \"mkdir_blocks\")?;\n        vfs.create_dir_all(&root.join(\"roots\"), \"mkdir_roots\")?;\n\n        let version_path = root.join(\"VERSION\");\n        match vfs.read(&version_path, \"read_version\") {\n            Ok(bytes) => {\n                if bytes != FORMAT_VERSION_LINE.as_bytes() {\n                    return Err(StoreError::BadMetadata {\n                        context: \"VERSION\".into(),\n                        detail: format!(\"unexpected contents: {:?}\", String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes)),\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => {\n                vfs.write_atomic(&version_path, FORMAT_VERSION_LINE.as_bytes(), \"rename_version\")?;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n        }\n\n        let store = Arc::new(Store {\n            root,\n            vfs,\n            pins: Arc::new(PinTable::new()),\n            upload: Mutex::new(()),\n            roots_lock: RwLock::new(()),\n            max_block_bytes: DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES,\n        });\n        store.cleanup_temp_files()?;\n        Ok(store)\n    }\n\n    pub fn data_dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.root\n    }\n\n    fn p(&self, rel: &Path) -> PathBuf {\n        self.root.join(rel)\n    }\n\n    /// Remove leftover staging files from interrupted writes (best effort).\n    fn cleanup_temp_files(&self) -> StoreResult<()> {\n        for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&self.p(Path::new(\"roots\")), \"list_roots\")? {\n            if entry.starts_with('.') {\n                let _ = self\n                    .vfs\n                    .remove_file(&self.p(Path::new(\"roots\")).join(&entry), \"cleanup_temp\");\n            }\n        }\n        for shard in self.vfs.list_dir(&self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\")), \"list_blocks\")? {\n            if shard.len() != 2 || !shard.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let shard_path = self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\")).join(&shard);\n            for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&shard_path, \"list_shard\")? {\n                if entry.starts_with('.') {\n                    let _ = self.vfs.remove_file(&shard_path.join(&entry), \"cleanup_temp\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    // ---------- blocks ----------\n\n    /// Store `data`. If `declared` is given it must match the actual SHA-256.\n    /// `refs` declares outgoing references (union with any prior sidecar);\n    /// references may point at blocks not yet uploaded (forward references).\n    pub fn put_block(\n        &self,\n        data: &[u8],\n        declared: Option<Sha256>,\n        refs: &[Sha256],\n    ) -> StoreResult<PutOutcome> {\n        if data.len() > self.max_block_bytes {\n            return Err(StoreError::TooLarge {\n                size: data.len(),\n                limit: self.max_block_bytes,\n            });\n        }\n        let hash = Sha256::hash(data);\n        if let Some(d) = declared {\n            if d != hash {\n                return Err(StoreError::HashMismatch {\n                    declared: d.to_hex(),\n                    actual: hash.to_hex(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        let _g = self.upload.lock().unwrap();\n        // Pin *before* the existence check: GC cannot remove the blob between\n        // our check and the durable write (sweep holds the same pin lock).\n        let _pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, hash);\n\n        let blob_path = self.p(&block_blob_rel(&hash));\n        let refs_path = self.p(&block_refs_rel(&hash));\n        let existed = self.vfs.exists(&blob_path, \"exists_block\")?;\n\n        if !existed {\n            self.vfs\n                .create_dir_all(blob_path.parent().unwrap(), \"mkdir_shard\")?;\n            self.vfs\n                .write_atomic(&blob_path, data, \"rename_block\")?;\n        }\n\n        let mut all: HashSet<Sha256> =\n            match self.vfs.read(&refs_path, \"read_refs\") {\n                Ok(bytes) => parse_refs_sidecar(&bytes, &hash.to_hex())?.into_iter().collect(),\n                Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => HashSet::new(),\n                Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n            };\n        let before = all.len();\n        all.extend(refs.iter().copied());\n\n        // Rewrite the sidecar whenever refs changed or when writing a fresh\n        // blob that was given refs.\n        if all.len() != before || (!existed && !all.is_empty()) {\n            let doc = build_refs_sidecar(&all);\n            self.vfs\n                .write_atomic(&refs_path, doc.as_bytes(), \"rename_block_refs\")?;\n        }\n\n        Ok(PutOutcome {\n            hash,\n            deduplicated: existed,\n            refs_count: all.len(),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Read a block, holding a GC pin for the duration and verifying the\n    /// digest of the bytes on disk.\n    pub fn get_block(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<Vec<u8>> {\n        let _pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, *hash);\n        let path = self.p(&block_blob_rel(hash));\n        let data = match self.vfs.read(&path, \"read_block\") {\n            Ok(d) => d,\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => {\n                return Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\"block {}\", hash.to_hex())))\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e.into()),\n        };\n        // Integrity verification: the digest is the content identity. A\n        // mismatch means bit rot or out-of-band tampering, never \"a different\n        // but acceptable block\".\n        if Sha256::hash(&data) != *hash {\n            return Err(StoreError::Corrupt {\n                hash: hash.to_hex(),\n                detail: \"stored bytes do not hash to their address\".into(),\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(data)\n    }\n\n    pub fn block_exists(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<bool> {\n        Ok(self\n            .vfs\n            .exists(&self.p(&block_blob_rel(hash)), \"exists_block\")?)\n    }\n\n    pub fn block_refs(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<Vec<Sha256>> {\n        match self.vfs.read(&self.p(&block_refs_rel(hash)), \"read_refs\") {\n            Ok(bytes) => parse_refs_sidecar(&bytes, &hash.to_hex()),\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => Ok(Vec::new()),\n            Err(e) => Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn block_info(&self, hash: &Sha256) -> StoreResult<Json> {\n        let present = self.block_exists(hash)?;\n        let refs = self.block_refs(hash)?;\n        let mut obj = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n        obj.insert(\"hash\".into(), Json::str(hash.to_hex()));\n        obj.insert(\"present\".into(), Json::Bool(present));\n        obj.insert(\n            \"refs\".into(),\n            Json::Arr(refs.iter().map(|r| Json::str(r.to_hex())).collect()),\n        );\n        Ok(Json::Obj(obj))\n    }\n\n    // ---------- roots ----------\n\n    /// Publish a root pointer atomically. `expected_version` implements\n    /// optimistic concurrency: the update succeeds only when the on-disk\n    /// version equals it (a missing root counts as version 0).\n    pub fn put_root(\n        &self,\n        name: &str,\n        hash: Sha256,\n        expected_version: Option<u64>,\n    ) -> StoreResult<RootRecord> {\n        validate_root_name(name)?;\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.write().unwrap();\n\n        // The target blob must exist. Pin it until the pointer is published so\n        // GC (which cannot run concurrently — same write lock — but defense in\n        // depth) cannot remove the block between check and publish.\n        let _pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, hash);\n        if !self.vfs.exists(&self.p(&block_blob_rel(&hash)), \"exists_block\")? {\n            return Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\n                \"block {} referenced by new root {name}\",\n                hash.to_hex()\n            )));\n        }\n\n        let path = self.p(&root_rel(name));\n        let current = self.read_root_locked(name)?;\n        let next_version = current.as_ref().map(|r| r.version + 1).unwrap_or(1);\n        if let Some(expected) = expected_version {\n            let actual = current.as_ref().map(|r| r.version).unwrap_or(0);\n            if expected != actual {\n                return Err(StoreError::VersionConflict {\n                    name: name.to_string(),\n                    expected,\n                    actual,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        let rec = RootRecord {\n            hash,\n            version: next_version,\n            updated_at_ms: now_ms(),\n        };\n        let doc = build_root_doc(&rec);\n        // Single atomic publish step. If this call fails (including an\n        // injected fault), no root file is created/modified: the old pointer\n        // stays readable and the new block is simply unreachable.\n        self.vfs.write_atomic(&path, doc.as_bytes(), \"rename_root\")?;\n        Ok(rec)\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_root(&self, name: &str) -> StoreResult<RootRecord> {\n        validate_root_name(name)?;\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.read().unwrap();\n        match self.read_root_locked(name)? {\n            Some(r) => Ok(r),\n            None => Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\"root {name}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn list_roots(&self) -> StoreResult<Vec<(String, RootRecord)>> {\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.read().unwrap();\n        self.list_roots_locked()\n    }\n\n    pub fn delete_root(&self, name: &str) -> StoreResult<bool> {\n        validate_root_name(name)?;\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.write().unwrap();\n        let path = self.p(&root_rel(name));\n        match self.vfs.remove_file(&path, \"delete_root\") {\n            Ok(()) => Ok(true),\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => Ok(false),\n            Err(e) => Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn read_root_locked(&self, name: &str) -> StoreResult<Option<RootRecord>> {\n        let path = self.p(&root_rel(name));\n        match self.vfs.read(&path, \"read_root\") {\n            Ok(bytes) => Ok(Some(parse_root_doc(&bytes, name)?)),\n            Err(e) if e.is_not_found() => Ok(None),\n            Err(e) => Err(e.into()),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn list_roots_locked(&self) -> StoreResult<Vec<(String, RootRecord)>> {\n        let mut out = Vec::new();\n        for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&self.p(Path::new(\"roots\")), \"list_roots\")? {\n            let Some(name) = entry.strip_suffix(\".json\") else {\n                continue;\n            };\n            if name.starts_with('.') {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if let Ok(Some(rec)) = self.read_root_locked(name) {\n                out.push((name.to_string(), rec));\n            }\n        }\n        out.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n\n    // ---------- GC ----------\n\n    /// Mark all blocks reachable from named roots through reference sidecars,\n    /// then sweep every unpinned blob. Root switches are blocked for the whole\n    /// operation; gets/uploads continue to work and their pins protect blocks.\n    pub fn gc(&self) -> StoreResult<GcReport> {\n        // Write lock: no root pointer may change during marking or sweeping.\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.write().unwrap();\n\n        let mut report = GcReport::default();\n\n        // ---- mark ----\n        let mut marked: HashSet<Sha256> = HashSet::new();\n        let mut queue: Vec<(Option<Sha256>, Sha256)> = Vec::new(); // (parent, child)\n\n        let roots = self.list_roots_locked()?;\n        report.roots_scanned = roots.len();\n        for (name, rec) in roots {\n            queue.push((None, rec.hash));\n            let _ = name;\n        }\n\n        while let Some((parent, hash)) = queue.pop() {\n            if marked.contains(&hash) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            // Pin immediately; un-pinned only after the sweep finishes.\n            let pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, hash);\n            let blob = self.p(&block_blob_rel(&hash));\n            let exists = match self.vfs.exists(&blob, \"exists_block\") {\n                Ok(b) => b,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    report.warnings.push(format!(\n                        \"cannot stat {}: {e}\",\n                        hash.to_hex()\n                    ));\n                    pin.disarm();\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n            if !exists {\n                report.missing_references.push(MissingReference {\n                    parent: parent.map(|p| p.to_hex()),\n                    missing: hash.to_hex(),\n                });\n                pin.disarm();\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Verify integrity of every reachable blob.\n            if let Ok(bytes) = self.vfs.read(&blob, \"read_block\") {\n                if Sha256::hash(&bytes) != hash {\n                    report.corrupt_blocks.push(hash.to_hex());\n                }\n            } else {\n                report\n                    .warnings\n                    .push(format!(\"cannot read {}\", hash.to_hex()));\n            }\n\n            marked.insert(hash);\n            pin.disarm_and_keep(&self.pins, hash); // bulk-unpin after sweep\n\n            for child in self.block_refs(&hash).unwrap_or_default() {\n                if !marked.contains(&child) {\n                    queue.push((Some(hash), child));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        report.blocks_live = marked.len();\n\n        // ---- sweep ----\n        let blocks_dir = self.p(Path::new(\"blocks\"));\n        let shards = self.vfs.list_dir(&blocks_dir, \"list_blocks\")?;\n        for shard in shards {\n            if shard.len() != 2 || !shard.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            let shard_path = blocks_dir.join(&shard);\n            for entry in self.vfs.list_dir(&shard_path, \"list_shard\")? {\n                if entry.starts_with('.') {\n                    // Stale staging file from a Pin it until the pointer is published so\n        // GC (which cannot run concurrently — same write lock — but defense in\n        // depth) cannot remove the block between check and publish.\n        let _pin = Pin::new(&self.pins, hash);\n        if !self.vfs.exists(&self.p(&block_blob_rel(&hash)), \"exists_block\")? {\n            return Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\n                \"block {} referenced by new root {name}\",\n                hash.to_hex()\n            )));\n        }\n\n        let path = self.p(&root_rel(name));\n        let current = self.read_root_locked(name)?;\n        let next_version = current.as_ref().map(|r| r.version + 1).unwrap_or(1);\n        if let Some(expected) = expected_version {\n            let actual = current.as_ref().map(|r| r.version).unwrap_or(0);\n            if expected != actual {\n                return Err(StoreError::VersionConflict {\n                    name: name.to_string(),\n                    expected,\n                    actual,\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        let rec = RootRecord {\n            hash,\n            version: next_version,\n            updated_at_ms: now_ms(),\n        };\n        let doc = build_root_doc(&rec);\n        // Single atomic publish step. If this call fails (including an\n        // injected fault), no root file is created/modified: the old pointer\n        // stays readable and the new block is simply unreachable.\n        self.vfs.write_atomic(&path, doc.as_bytes(), \"rename_root\")?;\n        Ok(rec)\n    }\n\n    pub fn get_root(&self, name: &str) -> StoreResult<RootRecord> {\n        validate_root_name(name)?;\n        let _g = self.roots_lock.read().unwrap();\n        match self.read_root_locked(name)? {\n            Some(r) => Ok(r),\n            None => Err(StoreError::NotFound(format!(\"root {name}\"))),\n        }","numLines":60,"startLine":468,"totalLines":868}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"33648640-2305-4ca4-ac23-c6de1cd33b45","session_id":"7cd997c3-1b91-495c-9d82-73da159982c0","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp5/a","sessionId":"7cd997c3-1b91-495c-9d82-73da159982c0","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp5-a","slug":"sprightly-chasing-valley"}

{"parentUuid":"b6abd63b-6129-4d1d-9d8f-adbf9d0a238f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_qxxwykh4pr2bmof6mlwu1017","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp5/a/src/server.rs","content":"//! Minimal dependency-free HTTP/1.1 verification entry point.\n//!\n//! This server exists to exercise the store over real sockets; it is not a\n//! production web server (thread per connection, no TLS, no auth).\n//!\n//! Routes\n//! ------\n//! ```text\n//! GET  /health\n//! POST /blocks                      raw body  OR  application/json {\"data_b64\": \"...\", \"hash\": \"...\", \"refs\": [\"...\"]}\n//! GET  /blocks/{hash}               raw bytes (digest re-verified)\n//! GET  /blocks/{hash}/info          metadata json\n//! PUT  /roots/{name}                raw hash in body OR json {\"hash\": \"...\"}\n//!                                    header If-Match: version N for OCC\n//! GET  /roots                       list\n//! GET  /roots/{name}                json\n//! DELETE /roots/{name}\n//! POST /gc                          run mark-sweep, report json\n//! GET  /stats\n//! ```\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::thread;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse crate::hash::Sha256;\nuse crate::json::Json;\nuse crate::store::{DynStore, StoreError};\n\npub struct Server {\n    listener: TcpListener,\n    store: Arc<DynStore>,\n    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ServerConfig {\n    pub read_timeout: Duration,\n    pub max_body_bytes: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Default for ServerConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        ServerConfig {\n            read_timeout: Duration::from_secs(30),\n            max_body_bytes: crate::store::DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Server {\n    /// Bind immediately so the chosen port is known before `serve` runs.\n    pub fn bind(addr: &str, store: Arc<DynStore>) -> std::io::Result<Self> {\n        let listener = TcpListener::bind(addr)?;\n        listener.set_nonblocking(true)?;\n        Ok(Server {\n            listener,\n            store,\n            stop: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn local_addr(&self) -> std::io::Result<std::net::SocketAddr> {\n        self.listener.local_addr()\n    }\n\n    pub fn shutdown_handle(&self) -> Arc<AtomicBool> {\n        self.stop.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Accept connections until `shutdown()` is called.\n    pub fn serve(self, cfg: ServerConfig) {\n        while !self.stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {\n            match self.listener.accept() {\n                Ok((stream, peer)) => {\n                    let store = self.store.clone();\n                    let stop = self.stop.clone();\n                    let cfg = ServerConfig { ..cfg };\n                    thread::spawn(move || {\n                        let _ = handle_connection(stream, peer, store, &stop, cfg);\n                    });\n                }\n                Err(ref e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {\n                    thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));\n                }\n                Err(_) => break,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn shutdown(&self) {\n        self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------- per-connection handling ----------------\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct Request {\n    method: String,\n    path: String,\n    headers: BTreeMap<String, String>,\n    body: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nfn handle_connection(\n    mut stream: TcpStream,\n    _peer: std::net::SocketAddr,\n    store: Arc<DynStore>,\n    stop: &AtomicBool,\n    cfg: ServerConfig,\n) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(cfg.read_timeout))?;\n    stream.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(30)))?;\n    let _ = stream.set_nodelay(true);\n\n    loop {\n        if stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let req = match read_request(&mut stream, cfg.max_body_bytes) {\n            Ok(Some(r)) => r,\n            Ok(None) => return Ok(()), // clean connection close\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof => return Ok(()),\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::TimedOut => return Ok(()),\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionReset => return Ok(()),\n            Err(_) => return Ok(()),\n        };\n        let keep_alive = req\n            .headers\n            .get(\"connection\")\n            .map(|v| !v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"close\"))\n            .unwrap_or(true);\n\n        let resp = route(&req, &store, &cfg);\n        write_response(&mut stream, &resp)?;\n        if !keep_alive {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn read_request(stream: &mut TcpStream, max_body: usize) -> std::io::Result<Option<Request>> {\n    let mut header_buf = Vec::new();\n    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];\n    loop {\n        match stream.read(&mut byte) {\n            Ok(0) if header_buf.is_empty() => return Ok(None),\n            Ok(0) => return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof, \"eof\")),\n            Ok(_) => {\n                header_buf.push(byte[0]);\n                if header_buf.len() >= 4 && &header_buf[header_buf.len() - 4..] == b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\" {\n                    break;\n                }\n                if header_buf.len() > 64 * 1024 {\n                    return Err(std::io::Error::new(\n                        std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"headers too large\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n            Err(ref e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&header_buf);\n    let mut lines = text.split(\"\\r\\n\");\n    let request_line = lines.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let mut parts = request_line.splitn(3, ' ');\n    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n    let raw_target = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    if method.is_empty() || raw_target.is_empty() {\n        return Err(std::io::Error::new(\n            std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n            \"bad request line\",\n        ));\n    }\n    let (path, query) = match raw_target.split_once('?') {\n        Some((p, q)) => (p.to_string(), q.to_string()),\n        None => (raw_target.to_string(), String::new()),\n    };\n\n    let mut headers = BTreeMap::new();\n    for line in lines {\n        if line.is_empty() {\n            break;\n        }\n        if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once(':') {\n            headers.insert(k.trim().to_ascii_lowercase(), v.trim().to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    let mut body = Vec::new();\n    if let Some(len_s) = headers.get(\"content-length\") {\n        let len: usize = len_s\n            .parse()\n            .map_err(|_| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, \"bad length\"))?;\n        if len > max_body {\n            return Err(std::io::Error::new(\n                std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                \"body too large\",\n            ));\n        }\n        body.resize(len, 0);\n        stream.read_exact(&mut body)?;\n    }\n\n    let _ = query; // parsed routes currently use path only\n    Ok(Some(Request {\n        method,\n        path,\n        headers,\n        body,\n    }))\n}\n\n// ---------------- responses ----------------\n\nstruct Response {\n    status: u16,\n    reason: &'static str,\n    content_type: &'static str,\n    body: Vec<u8>,\n    extra_headers: Vec<(String, String)>,\n}\n\nimpl Response {\n    fn json(status: u16, reason: &'static str, value: &Json) -> Self {\n        Response {\n            status,\n            reason,\n            content_type: \"application/json; charset=utf-8\",\n            body: value.to_compact_string().into_bytes(),\n            extra_headers: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn error(status: u16, reason: &'static str, code: &str, message: &str) -> Self {\n        let mut obj = BTreeMap::new();\n        obj.insert(\"error\".into(), Json::str(code));\n        obj.insert(\"message\".into(), Json::str(message));\n        Self::json(status, reason, &Json::Obj(obj))\n    }\n\n    fn bytes(status: u16, reason: &'static str, body: Vec<u8>, content_type: &str) -> Self {\n        Response {\n            status,\n            reason,\n            content_type,\n            body,\n            extra_headers: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn write_response(stream: &mut TcpStream, resp: &Response) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    let mut head = format!(\n        \"HTTP/1.1 {} {}\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nContent-Type: {}\\r\\nConnection: keep-alive\\r\\n\",\n        resp.status,\n        resp.reason,\n        resp.body.len(),\n        resp.content_type\n    );\n    for (k, v) in &resp.extra_headers {\n        head.push_str(k);\n        head.push_str(\": \");\n        head.push_str(v);\n        head.push_str(\"\\r\\n\");\n    }\n    head.push_str(\"\\r\\n\");\n    stream.write_all(head.as_bytes())?;\n    stream.write_all(&resp.body)?;\n    stream.flush()\n}\n\n// ---------------- routing ----------------\n\nfn route(req: &Request, store: &Arc<DynStore>, cfg: &ServerConfig) -> Response {\n    let path = req.path.as_str();\n    let method = req.method.as_str();\n\n    match (method, path) {\n        (\"GET\", \"/health\") => {\n            let mut obj = BTreeMap::new();\n            obj.insert(\"status\".into(), Json::str(\"ok\"));\n            Response::json(200, \"OK\", &Json::Obj(obj))\n        }\n        (\"GET\", \"/stats\") => match store.stats() {\n            Ok(s) => {\n                let mut obj = BTreeMap::new();\n                obj.insert(\"roots\".into(), Json::from_u64(s.roots as u64));\n                obj.insert(\"blocks\".into(), Json::from_u64(s.blocks as u64));\n                obj.insert(\"block_bytes\".into(), Json::from_u64(s.block_bytes));\n                Response::json(200, \"OK\", &Json::Obj(obj))\n            }\n            Err(e) => store_err(e),\n        },\n        (\"POST\", \"/gc\") => match store.gc() {\n            Ok(rep) => {\n                let status = if rep.missing_references.is_empty() && rep.corrupt_blocks.is_empty()\n                {\n                    200\n                } else {\n                    200\n                };\n                Response::json(status, \"OK\", &gc_report_json(&rep))\n            }\n            Err(e) => store_err(e),\n        },\n        (\"POST\", \"/blocks\") => put_block_handler(req, store, cfg),\n        (\"GET\", p) if p.starts_with(\"/blocks/\") => {\n            let rest = &p[\"/blocks/\".len()..];\n            if let Some(hash_hex) = rest.strip_suffix(\"/info\") {\n                match crate::store::parse_hash(hash_hex) {\n                    Ok(h) => match store.block_info(&h) {\n                        Ok(v) => Response::json(200, \"OK\", &v),\n                        Err(e) => as u8;\n    }\n    let bytes = input.as_bytes();\n    if bytes.len() % 4 != 0 {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len() / 4 * 3);\n    let mut chunk = 0u32;\n    let mut bits = 0u32;\n    let mut padding = 0;\n    for (i, &b) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {\n        if b == b'=' {\n            padding += 1;\n            if padding > 2 || i < bytes.len() - 2 {\n Minimal dependency-free HTTP/1.1 verification entry point.\n//!\n//! This server exists to exercise the store over real sockets; it is not a\n//! production web server (thread per connection, no TLS, no auth).\n//!\n//! Routes\n//! ------\n//! ```text\n//! GET  /health\n//! POST /blocks                      raw body  OR  application/json {\"data_b64\": \"...\", \"hash\": \"...\", \"refs\": [\"...\"]}\n//! GET  /blocks/{hash}               raw bytes (digest re-verified)\n//! GET  /blocks/{hash}/info          metadata json\n//! PUT  /roots/{name}                raw hash in body OR json {\"hash\": \"...\"}\n//!                                    header If-Match: version N for OCC\n//! GET  /roots                       list\n//! GET  /roots/{name}                json\n//! DELETE /roots/{name}\n//! POST /gc                          run mark-sweep, report json\n//! GET  /stats\n//! ```\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::thread;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse crate::hash::Sha256;\nuse crate::json::Json;\nuse crate::store::{DynStore, StoreError};\n\npub struct Server {\n    listener: TcpListener,\n    store: Arc<DynStore>,\n    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ServerConfig {\n    pub read_timeout: Duration,\n    pub max_body_bytes: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Default for ServerConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        ServerConfig {\n            read_timeout: Duration::from_secs(30),\n            max_body_bytes: crate::store::DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Server {\n    /// Bind immediately so the chosen port is known before `serve` runs.\n    pub fn bind(addr: &str, store: Arc<DynStore>) -> std::io::Result<Self> {\n        let listener = TcpListener::bind(addr)?;\n        listener.set_nonblocking(true)?;\n        Ok(Server {\n            listener,\n            store,\n            stop: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn local_addr(&self) -> std::io::Result<std::net::SocketAddr> {\n        self.listener.local_addr()\n    }\n\n    pub fn shutdown_handle(&self) -> Arc<AtomicBool> {\n        self.stop.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Accept connections until `shutdown()` is called.\n    pub fn serve(self, cfg: ServerConfig) {\n        while !self.stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {\n            match self.listener.accept() {\n                Ok((stream, peer)) => {\n                    let store = self.store.clone();\n                    let stop = self.stop.clone();\n                    let cfg = ServerConfig { ..cfg };\n                    thread::spawn(move || {\n                        let _ = handle_connection(stream, peer, store, &stop, cfg);\n                    });\n                }\n                Err(ref e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {\n                    thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));\n                }\n                Err(_) => break,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn shutdown(&self) {\n        self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------- per-connection handling ----------------\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct Request {\n    method: String,\n    path: String,\n    headers: BTreeMap<String, String>,\n    body: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nfn handle_connection(\n    mut stream: TcpStream,\n    _peer: std::net::SocketAddr,\n    store: Arc<DynStore>,\n    stop: &AtomicBool,\n    cfg: ServerConfig,\n) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(cfg.read_timeout))?;\n    stream.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(30)))?;\n    let _ = stream.set_nodelay(true);\n\n    loop {\n        if stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let req = match read_request(&mut stream, cfg.max_body_bytes) {\n            Ok(Some(r)) => r,\n            Ok(None) => return Ok(()), // clean connection close\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof => return Ok(()),\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::TimedOut => return Ok(()),\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionReset => return Ok(()),\n            Err(_) => return Ok(()),\n        };\n        let keep_alive = req\n            .headers\n            .get(\"connection\")\n            .map(|v| !v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"close\"))\n            .unwrap_or(true);\n\n        let resp = route(&req, &store, &cfg);\n        write_response(&mut stream, &resp)?;\n        if !keep_alive {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn read_request(stream: &mut TcpStream, max_body: usize) -> std::io::Result<Option<Request>> {\n    let mut header_buf = Vec::new();\n    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];\n    loop {\n        match stream.read(&mut byte) {\n            Ok(0) if header_buf.is_empty() => return Ok(None),\n            Ok(0) => return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof, \"eof\")),\n            Ok(_) => {\n                header_buf.push(byte[0]);\n                if header_buf.len() >= 4 && &header_buf[header_buf.len() - 4..] == b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\" {\n                    break;\n                }\n                if header_buf.len() > 64 * 1024 {\n                    return Err(std::io::Error::new(\n                        std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"headers too large\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n            Err(ref e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&header_buf);\n    let mut lines = text.split(\"\\r\\n\");\n    let request_line = lines.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let mut parts = request_line.splitn(3, ' ');\n    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n    let raw_target = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    if method.is_empty() || raw_target.is_empty() {\n        return Err(std::io::Error::new(\n            std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n            \"bad request line\",\n        ));\n    }\n    let (path, query) = match raw_target.split_once('?') {\n        Some((p, q)) => (p.to_string(), q.to_string()),\n        None => (raw_target.to_string(), String::new()),\n    };\n\n    let mut headers = BTreeMap::new();\n    for line in lines {\n        if line.is_empty() {\n            break;\n        }\n        if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once(':') {\n            headers.insert(k.trim().to_ascii_lowercase(), v.trim().to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    let mut body = Vec::new();\n    if let Some(len_s) = headers.get(\"content-length\") {\n        let len: usize = len_s\n            .parse()\n            .map_err(|_| std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, \"bad length\"))?;\n        if len > max_body {\n            return Err(std::io::Error::new(\n                std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                \"body too large\",\n            ));\n        }\n        body.resize(len, 0);\n        stream.read_exact(&mut body)?;\n    }\n\n    let _ = query; // parsed routes currently use path only\n    Ok(Some(Request {\n        method,\n        path,\n        headers,\n        body,\n    }))\n}\n\n// ---------------- responses ----------------\n\nstruct Response {\n    status: u16,\n    reason: &'static str,\n    content_type: &'static str,\n    body: Vec<u8>,\n    extra_headers: Vec<(String, String)>,\n}\n\nimpl Response {\n    fn json(status: u16, reason: &'static str, value: &Json) -> Self {\n        Response {\n            status,\n            reason,\n            content_type: \"application/json; charset=utf-8\",\n            body: value.to_compact_string().into_bytes(),\n            extra_headers: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn error(status: u16, reason: &'static str, code: &str, message: &str) -> Self {\n        let mut obj = BTreeMap::new();\n        obj.insert(\"error\".into(), Json::str(code));\n        obj.insert(\"message\".into(), Json::str(message));\n        Self::json(status, reason, &Json::Obj(obj))\n    }\n\n    fn bytes(status: u16, reason: &'static str, body: Vec<u8>, content_type: &str) -> Self {\n        Response {\n            status,\n            reason,\n            content_type,\n            body,\n            extra_headers: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn write_response(stream: &mut TcpStream, resp: &Response) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    let mut head = format!(\n        \"HTTP/1.1 {} {}\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nContent-Type: {}\\r\\nConnection: keep-alive\\r\\n\",\n        resp.status,\n        resp.reason,\n        resp.body.len(),\n        resp.content_type\n    );\n    for (k, v) in &resp.extra_headers {\n        head.push_str(k);\n        head.push_str(\": \");\n        head.push_str(v);\n        head.push_str(\"\\r\\n\");\n    }\n    head.push_str(\"\\r\\n\");\n    stream.write_all(head.as_bytes())?;\n    stream.write_all(&resp.body)?;\n    stream.flush()\n}\n\n// ---------------- routing ----------------\n\nfn route(req: &Request, store: &Arc<DynStore>, cfg: &ServerConfig) -> Response {\n    let path = req.path.as_str();\n    let method = req.method.as_str();\n\n    match (method, path) {\n        (\"GET\", \"/health\") => {\n            let mut obj = BTreeMap::new();\n            obj.insert(\"status\".into(), Json::str(\"ok\"));\n            Response::json(200, \"OK\", &Json::Obj(obj))\n        }\n        (\"GET\", \"/stats\") => match store.stats() {\n            Ok(s) => {\n                let mut obj = BTreeMap::new();\n                obj.insert(\"roots\".into(), Json::from_u64(s.roots as u64));\n                obj.insert(\"blocks\".into(), Json::from_u64(s.blocks as u64));\n                obj.insert(\"block_bytes\".into(), Json::from_u64(s.block_bytes));\n                Response::json(200, \"OK\", &Json::Obj(obj))\n            }\n            Err(e) => store_err(e),\n        },\n        (\"POST\", \"/gc\") => match store.gc() {\n            Ok(rep) => {\n                let status = if rep.missing_references.is_empty() && GET  /health\n//! POST /blocks                      raw body  OR  application/json {\"data_b64\": \"...\", \"hash\": \"...\", \"refs\": [\"...\"]}\n//! GET  /blocks/{hash}               raw bytes (digest re-verified)\n//! GET  /blocks/{hash}/info          metadata json\n//! GET  /stats\n//! ```\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse Arc<DynStore>,\n    stop: Arc<AtomicBool>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ServerConfig {\n    pub read_timeout: Duration,\n    pub max_body_bytes: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Default for ServerConfig {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        ServerConfig {\n            read_timeout: Duration::from_secs(30),\n            max_body_bytes: crate::store::DEFAULT_MAX_BLOCK_BYTES,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Server {\n    /// Bind immediately so the chosen port is known before `serve` runs.\n    pub fn bind(addr: &str, store: Arc<DynStore>) -> std::io::Result<Self> {\n        let listener = TcpListener::bind(addr)?;\n        listener.set_nonblocking(true)?;\n        Ok(Server {\n            listener,\n            store,\n            stop: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn local_addr(&self) -> std::io::Result<std::net::SocketAddr> {\n        self.listener.local_addr()\n    }\n\n    pub fn shutdown_handle(&self) -> Arc<AtomicBool> {\n        self.stop.clone()\n    }\n\n    /// Accept connections until `shutdown()` is called.\n    pub fn serve(self, cfg: ServerConfig) {\n        while !self.stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {\n            match self.listener.accept() {\n                Ok((stream, peer)) => {\n                    let store = self.store.clone();\n                    let stop = self.stop.clone();\n                    let cfg = ServerConfig { ..cfg };\n                    thread::spawn(move || {\n                        let _ = handle_connection(stream, peer, store, &stop, cfg);\n                    });\n                }\n                Err(ref e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {\n                    thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10));\n                }\n                Err(_) => break,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn shutdown(&self) {\n        self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------- per-connection handling ----------------\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct Request {\n    method: String,\n    path: String,\n    headers: BTreeMap<String, String>,\n    body: Vec<u8>,\n}\n\nfn handle_connection(\n    mut stream: TcpStream,\n    _peer: std::net::SocketAddr,\n    store: Arc<DynStore>,\n    stop: &AtomicBool,\n    cfg: ServerConfig,\n) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(cfg.read_timeout))?;\n    stream.set_write_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(30)))?;\n    let _ = stream.set_nodelay(true);\n\n    loop {\n        if stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n        let req = match read_request(&mut stream, cfg.max_body_bytes) {\n            Ok(Some(r)) => r,\n            Ok(None) => return Ok(()), // clean connection close\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof => return Ok(()),\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::TimedOut => return Ok(()),\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionReset => return Ok(()),\n            Err(_) => return Ok(()),\n        };\n        let keep_alive = req\n            .headers\n            .get(\"connection\")\n            .map(|v| !v.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"close\"))\n            .unwrap_or(true);\n\n        let resp = route(&req, &store, &cfg);\n        write_response(&mut stream, &resp)?;\n        if !keep_alive {\n            return Ok(());\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn read_request(stream: &mut TcpStream, max_body: usize) -> std::io::Result<Option<Request>> {\n    let mut header_buf = Vec::new();\n    let mut byte = [0u8; 1];\n    loop {\n        match stream.read(&mut byte) {\n            Ok(0) if header_buf.is_empty() => return Ok(None),\n            Ok(0) => return Err(std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof, \"eof\")),\n            Ok(_) => {\n                header_buf.push(byte[0]);\n                if header_buf.len() >= 4 && &header_buf[header_buf.len() - 4..] == b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\" {\n                    break;\n                }\n                if header_buf.len() > 64 * 1024 {\n                    return Err(std::io::Error::new(\n                        std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"headers too large\",\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n            Err(ref e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&header_buf);\n    let mut lines = text.split(\"\\r\\n\");\n    let request_line = lines.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let mut parts = request_line.splitn(3, ' ');\n    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n    let raw_target = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    if method.is_empty() || raw_target.is_empty() {\n        return Err(std::io::Error::new(\n            std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n            \"bad request line\",\n        ));\n    }\n    let (path, query) = match raw_target.split_once('?') {\n        Some((p, q)) => (p.to_string(), q.to_string()),\n        None => (raw_target.to_string(), String::new()),\n    };\n\n    let mut headers = BTreeMap::new();\n    for line in lines {\n        if line.is_empty() {\n            break;\n        }\n        if let Some((k, v)) = line.split_once(':') {\n            headers.insert(k.trim().to_ascii_lowercase(), v.trim().to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    let mut body = Vec::new();\n length\"))?;\n        if len > max_body {\n            return Err(std::io::Error::new(\n                std::io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                \"body too large\",\n            ));\n        }\n        body.resize(len, 0);\n        stream.read_exact(&mut body)?;\n    }\n\n    let _ = query; // parsed routes currently use path only\n    Ok(Some(Request {\n        method,\n        path,\n        headers,\n        body,\n    }))\n}\n\n// ---------------- responses ----------------\n\nstruct Response {\n    status: u16,\n    reason: &'static str,\n    content_type: &'static str,\n    body: Vec<u8>,\n    extra_headers: Vec<(String, String)>,\n}\n\nimpl Response {\n    fn json(status: u16, reason: &'static str, value: &Json) -> Self {\n        Response {\n            status,\n            reason,\n            content_type: \"application/json; charset=utf-8\",\n            body: value.to_compact_string().into_bytes(),\n            extra_headers: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn error(status: u16, reason: &'static str, code: &str, message: &str) -> Self {\n        let mut obj = BTreeMap::new();\n        obj.insert(\"error\".into(), Json::str(code));\n        obj.insert(\"message\".into(), Json::str(message));\n        Self::json(status, reason, &Json::Obj(obj))\n    }\n\n    fn bytes(status: u16, reason: &'static str, body: Vec<u8>, content_type: &str) -> Self {\n        Response {\n            status,\n            reason,\n            content_type,\n            body,\n            extra_headers: Vec::new(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn write_response(stream: &mut TcpStream, resp: &Response) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    let mut head = format!(\n        \"HTTP/1.1 {} {}\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nContent-Type: {}\\r\\nConnection: cas_repo::server::{Server, ServerConfig};\nuse cas_repo::store::DynStore;\nuse cas_repo::vfs::{StdVfs, Vfs};\n\nfn print_usage() {\n    eprintln!(\n        \"cas-repo — content-addressable block repository\\n\\\n\\n\\\nUSAGE:\\n    cas-repo serve --data <DATA_DIR> [--addr 127.0.0.1:8080]\\n\"\n    );\n}\n\nfn main() -> ExitCode {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();\n    let mut data: Option<PathBuf> = None;\n    let mut addr = \"127.0.0.1:8080\".to_string();\n    let mut iter = args.iter();\n    while let Some(a) = iter.next() {\n        match a.as_str() {\n            \"serve\" => {}\n            \"--data\" | \"-d\" => data = iter.next().map(PathBuf::from),\n            \"--addr\" | \"-a\" => {\n                if let Some(v) = iter.next() {\n                    addr = v.clone();\n                }\n            }\n            \"-h\" | \"--help\" => {\n                print_usage();\n                return ExitCode::SUCCESS;\n            }\n            other => {\n                eprintln!(\"unknown argument: {other}\");\n                print_usage();\n                return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    let data = match data {\n        Some(d) => d,\n        None => {\n            eprintln!(\"missing --data <DATA_DIR>\");\n            print_usage();\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n\n    let vfs: Box<dyn Vfs> = Box::new(StdVfs::new());\n    let store: Arc<DynStore> = match DynStore::open_boxed(&data, vfs) {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"failed to open store at {}: {e}\", data.display());\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n\n    let server = match Server::bind(&addr, store) {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"failed to bind {addr}: {e}\");\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n    let bound = server.local_addr().unwrap();\n    eprintln!(\"cas-repo listening on http://{bound} (data: {})\", data.display());\n\n    // Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM.\n    let stop = server.shutdown_handle();\n    install_signal_handler(stop);\n\n    server.serve(ServerConfig::default());\n    eprintln!(\"cas-repo stopped\");\n    ExitCode::SUCCESS\n}\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn install_signal_handler(stop: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>) {\n    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;\n    unsafe {\n        extern \"C\" fn handler(_: i32) {\n            // Signal handler only flags shutdown; the accept loop polls.\n        }\n        let _ = handler;\n    }\n    // A dedicated thread waits on sigwait-style semantics via the simple\n    // self-pipe alternative: just install a default-ish handler using\n    // libc-free std by spawning a thread that polls a flag file descriptor is\n    // not portable; instead rely on Ctrl-C terminating with connection\n    // draining being best effort. For cleaner behavior, catch SIGINT through\n    // the `signal-hook`-free approach below.\n    thread_set_ctrlc(stop, Ordering::Relaxed);\n}\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn thread_set_ctrlc(stop: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>, _ord: std::sync::atomic::Ordering) {\n    // Minimal SIGINT/SIGTERM handling via raw libc bindings would pull in a\n    // dependency; instead spawn a thread reading from stdin is unsuitable for\n    // servers. We use the POSIX API through a tiny extern block.\n    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;\n    unsafe extern \"C\" fn on_sig(_sig: i32) {\n        // Async-signal-safe: do nothing; the accept loop times out? It is\n        // non-blocking with a 10ms poll, but the main thread is blocked in\n        // serve(). To interrupt, set the flag through a static.\n        SHUTDOWN.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);\n    }\n    static SHUTDOWN: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool = std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);\n\n    // Link the static to the passed handle: the poll in serve() checks its own\n    // flag, so make the signal thread flip the real Arc by watching the static\n    // from another thread.\n    extern \"C\" {\n        fn signal(signum: i32, handler: unsafe extern \"C\" fn(i32)) -> usize;\n    }\n    unsafe {\n        signal(2 /* SIGINT */, on_sig);\n        signal(15 /* SIGTERM */, on_sig);\n    }\n    let stop2 = stop;\n    std::thread::spawn(move || loop {\n        if SHUTDOWN.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {\n            stop2.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);\n            break;\n        }\n        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(20));\n    });\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn install_signal_handler(_stop: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>) {}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_88f9c6fc8da0176c593c1c73","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":382,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":70456,"output_tokens":1438,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_p0t2kfy24utphjc6ormsj3jc":{"content":"//! Command-line entry point:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! cas-repo serve --data <dir> --addr 127.0.0.1:8080\n//! ```\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::ExitCode;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse cas_repo::server::{Server, ServerConfig};\nuse cas_repo::store::DynStore;\nuse cas_repo::vfs::{StdVfs, Vfs};\n\nfn print_usage() {\n    eprintln!(\n        \"cas-repo — content-addressable block repository\\n\\\n\\n\\\nUSAGE:\\n    cas-repo serve --data <DATA_DIR> [--addr 127.0.0.1:8080]\\n\"\n    );\n}\n\nfn main() -> ExitCode {\n    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();\n    let mut data: Option<PathBuf> = None;\n    let mut addr = \"127.0.0.1:8080\".to_string();\n    let mut iter = args.iter();\n    while let Some(a) = iter.next() {\n        match a.as_str() {\n            \"serve\" => {}\n            \"--data\" | \"-d\" => data = iter.next().map(PathBuf::from),\n            \"--addr\" | \"-a\" => {\n                if let Some(v) = iter.next() {\n                    addr = v.clone();\n                }\n            }\n            \"-h\" | \"--help\" => {\n                print_usage();\n                return ExitCode::SUCCESS;\n            }\n            other => {\n                eprintln!(\"unknown argument: {other}\");\n                print_usage();\n                return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    let data = match data {\n        Some(d) => d,\n        None => {\n            eprintln!(\"missing --data <DATA_DIR>\");\n            print_usage();\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n\n    let vfs: Box<dyn Vfs> = Box::new(StdVfs::new());\n    let store: Arc<DynStore> = match DynStore::open_boxed(&data, vfs) {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"failed to open store at {}: {e}\", data.display());\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n\n    let server = match Server::bind(&addr, store) {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"failed to bind {addr}: {e}\");\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n    let bound = server.local_addr().unwrap();\n    eprintln!(\"cas-repo listening on http://{bound} (data: {})\", data.display());\n\n    // Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM.\n    let stop = server.shutdown_handle();\n    install_signal_handler(stop);\n\n    server.serve(ServerConfig::default());\n    eprintln!(\"cas-repo stopped\");\n    ExitCode::SUCCESS\n}\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn install_signal_handler(stop: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>) {\n    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;\n    unsafe {\n        extern \"C\" fn handler(_: i32) {\n            // Signal handler only flags shutdown; the accept loop polls.\n        }\n        let _ = handler;\n    }\n    // A dedicated thread waits on sigwait-style semantics via the simple\n    // self-pipe alternative: just install a default-ish handler using\n    // libc-free std by spawning a thread that polls a flag file descriptor is\n    // not portable; instead rely on Ctrl-C terminating with connection\n    // draining being best effort. For cleaner behavior, catch SIGINT through\n    // the `signal-hook`-free approach below.\n    thread_set_ctrlc(stop, Ordering::Relaxed);\n}\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn thread_set_ctrlc(stop: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool>, _ord: std::sync::atomic::Ordering) {\n    // Minimal SIGINT/SIGTERM handling via raw libc bindings would pull in a\n    // dependency; instead spawn a thread reading from stdin is unsuitable for\n    // servers. We use the POSIX API through a tiny extern block.\n    use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;\n    unsafe extern \"C\" fn on_sig(_sig: i32) {\n        // Async-signal-safe: do nothing; the accept loop times out? The digest never acts as an\n//! authorization capability.\n\n/// 32-byte SHA-256 digest.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq)]\npub struct Sha256(pub [u8; 32]);\n\nconst K: [u32; 64] = [\n  0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786, 0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc, 0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da,\n    0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7, 0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967,\n    0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13, 0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85,\n    0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b, 0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3, 0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070,\n    0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5, 0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a, 0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3,\n    0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208, 0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7, 0xc67178f2,\n];\n\npub struct Sha256Ctx {\n    h: [u32; 8],\n    len: u64,\n    buf: [u8; 64],\n    buf_len: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Sha256Ctx {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Sha256Ctx {\n            h: [\n                0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab,\n                0x5be0cd19,\n            ],\n            len: 0,\n            buf: [0; 64],\n            buf_len: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn update(&mut self, data: &[u8]) {\n        self.len = self.len.wrapping_add(data.len() as u64);\n        let mut data = data;\n        if self.buf_len > 0 {\n            let take = (64 - self.buf_len).min(data.len());\n            self.buf[self.buf_len..self.buf_len + take].copy_from_slice(&data[..take]);\n            self.buf_len += take;\n            data = &data[take..];\n            if self.buf_len == 64 {\n                let block = self.buf;\n                self.compress(&block);\n                self.buf_len = 0;\n            }\n        }\n        while data.len() >= 64 {\n            let mut block = [0u8; 64];\n            block.copy_from_slice(&data[..64]);\n            self.compress(&block);\n            data = &data[64..];\n        }\n        if !data.is_empty() {\n            self.buf[..data.len()].copy_from_slice(data);\n            self.buf_len = data.len();\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn finish(mut self) -> Sha256 {\n        let bit_len = self.len.wrapping_mul(8);\n        self.buf[self.buf_len] = 0x80;\n        for b in &mut self.buf[self.buf_len + 1..] {\n            *b = 0;\n        }\n        if self.buf_len >= 56 {\n            let block = self.buf;\n            self.compress(&block);\n            self.buf = [0; 64];\n        }\n        self.buf[56..64].copy_from_slice(&bit_len.to_be_bytes());\n        let block = self.buf;\n        self.compress(&block);\n        let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n        for (i, word) in self.h.iter().enumerate() {\n            out[i * 4..i * 4 + 4].copy_from_slice(&word.to_be_bytes());\n        }\n        Sha256(out)\n    }\n\n    fn compress(&mut self, block: &[u8; 64]) {\n        let mut w = [0u32; 64];\n        for i in 0..16 {\n            w[i] = u32::from_be_bytes([\n                block[i * 4],\n                block[i * 4 + 1],\n                block[i * 4 + 2],\n                block[i * 4 + 3],\n            ]);\n        }\n        for i in 16..64 {\n            let s0 = w[i - 15].rotate_right(7) ^ w[i - 15].rotate_right(18) ^ (w[i - 15] >> 3);\n            let s1 = w[i - 2].rotate_right(17) ^ w[i - 2].rotate_right(19) ^ (w[i - 2] >> 10);\n            w[i] = w[i - 16]\n                .wrapping_add(s0)\n                .wrapping_add(w[i - 7])\n                .wrapping_add(s1);\n        }\n        let (mut a, mut b, mut c, mut d) = (self.h[0], self.h[1], self.h[2], self.h[3]);\n        let (mut e, mut f, mut g, mut hh) = (self.h[4], self.h[5], self.h[6], self.h[7]);\n        for i in 0..64 {\n            let s1 = e.rotate_right(6) ^ e.rotate_right(11) ^ e.rotate_right(25);\n            let ch = (e & f) ^ ((!e) & g);\n            let t1 = hh\n a.rotate_right(22);\n            let maj = (a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c);\n            let t2 = s0.wrapping_add(maj);\n            hh = g;\n            g = f;\n            f = e;\n            e = d.wrapping_add(t1);\n            d = c;\n            c = b;\n            b = a;\n            a = t1.wrapping_add(t2);\n        }\n        self.h[0] = self.h[0].wrapping_add(a);\n        self.h[1] = self.h[1].wrapping_add(b);\n        self.h[2] = self.h[2].wrapping_add(c);\n        self.h[3] = self.h[3].wrapping_add(d);\n        self.h[4] = self.h[4].wrapping_add(e);\n        self.h[5] = self.h[5].wrapping_add(f);\n        self.h[6] = self.h[6].wrapping_add(g);\n        self.h[7] = self.h[7].wrapping_add(hh);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sha256 {\n    pub fn hash(data: &[u8]) -> Self {\n        let mut ctx = Sha256Ctx::new();\n        ctx.update(data);\n        ctx.finish()\n    }\n\n    pub fn to_hex(&self) -> String {\n        let mut s = String::with_capacity(64);\n        for b in &self.0 {\n            s.push(hex_nibble(b >> 4));\n            s.push(hex_nibble(b & 0xf));\n        }\n        s\n    }\n\n    pub fn from_hex(s: &str) -> Option<Self> {\n        let b = s.as_bytes();\n        if b.len() != 64 {\n            return None;\n        }\n        let mut out = [0u8; 32];\n        for i in 0..32 {\n            let hi = hex_val(b[i * 2])?;\n            let lo = hex_val(b[i * 2 + 1])?;\n            out[i] = (hi << 4) | lo;\n        }\n        Some(Sha256(out))\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; 32] {\n        &self.0\n    }\n}\n\nfn hex_nibble(n: u8) -> char {\n    match n {\n        0..=9 => (b'0' + n) as char,\n        _ => (b'a' + (n - 10)) as char,\n    }\n}\n\nfn hex_val(c: u8) -> Option<u8> {\n    match c {\n        b'0'..=b'9' => Some(c - b'0'),\n        b'a'..=b'f' => Some(c - b'a' + 10),\n        b'A'..=b'F' => Some(c - b'A' + 10),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn known_vectors() {\n        // NIST FIPS 180-4 examples.\n        assert_eq!(\n            Sha256::hash(b\"abc\").to_hex(),\n            \"ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad\"\n        );\n        assert_eq!(\n            Sha256::hash(b\"\").to_hex(),\n            \"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855\"\n        );\n        let million_a = vec![b'a'; 1_000_000];\n        assert_eq!(\n            Sha256::hash(&million_a).to_hex(),\n vec![0x5au8; 200];\n        for split in 0..=200 {\n            let mut ctx = Sha256Ctx::new();\n            ctx.update(&data[..split]);\n            ctx.update(&data[split..]);\n Shared helpers for integration tests.\n\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};\n\n/// Self-deleting temporary directory for one test.\npub struct TempDir(pub PathBuf);\n\nimpl TempDir {\n    pub fn new(tag: &str) -> Self {\n        static COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);\n        let n = COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);\n        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(\n            \"cas-repo-test-{}-{}-{n}\",\n            std::process::id(),\n            tag\n        ));\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();\n        TempDir(dir)\n    }\n\n    pub fn path(&self) -> &std::path::Path {\n        &self.0\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for TempDir {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Standard-alphabet base64 encoder (tests only).\npub fn b64_encode(data: &[u8]) -> String {\n    const T: &[u8; 64] = b\"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/\";\n    let mut out = String::new();\n    for chunk in data.chunks(3) {\n        let b = [\n            chunk[0],\n            *chunk.get(1).unwrap_or(&0),\n            *chunk.get(2).unwrap_or(&0),\n        ];\n        let n = ((b[0] as u32) << 16) | ((b[1] as u32) << 8) | b[2] as u32;\n        out.push(T[(n >> 18) as usize & 63] as char);\n        out.push(T[(n >> 12) as usize & 63] as char);\n        out.push(if chunk.len() > 1 {\n            T[(n >> 6) as usize & 63] as char\n        } else {\n            '='\n        });\n        out.push(if chunk.len() > 2 {\n            T[n as usize & 63] as char\n        } else {\n            '='\n        });\n    }\n    out\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_a88851111ce1a7171b85c83a","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":115,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":73728,"output_tokens":1687,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_26e9cc297200459fa2afceb4":{"content":"//! 64] = b\"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/\";\n    let mut out = String::new();\n    for chunk in data.chunks(3) {\n        let b = [\n            chunk[0],\n            *chunk.get(1).unwrap_or(&0),\n            *chunk.get(2).unwrap_or(&0),\n        ];\n        let n = ((b[0] as u32) << 16) | ((b[1] as u32) << 8) | b[2] as u32;\n        out.push(T[(n >> 18) as usize & 63] as char);\n        out.push(T[(n >> 12) as usize & 63] as char);\n        out.push(if chunk.len() > 1 {\n            T[(n >> 6) as usize & 63] as char\n        } else {\n            '='\n        });\n        out.push(if chunk.len() > 2 {\n            T[n as usize & 63] as char\n        } else {\n            '='\n        });\n    }\n    out\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"a027c08b-fef2-478f-8ac4-b29f72ee5110","session_id":"7cd997c3-1b91-495c-9d82-73da159982c0","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp5/a","sessionId":"7cd997c3-1b91-495c-9d82-73da159982c0","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp5-a","slug":"sprightly-chasing-valley"}
